entry.title: Palm Beach Royals ambassadors bring pickleball to the Boys & Girls Clubs of Palm Beach County
entry.summary: The fastest-growing sport in the world just got more players. This week, the middle and high school students in Palm Beach County got to try pickleball for the first time. On Wednesday, the Palm Beach Royals , South Florida's Major League Pickleball team, brought the sport to Boys Girls Clubs across the county. WATCH BELOW: Palm Beach Royals bring pickleball to Boys Girls Clubs Palm Beach Royals bring pickleball to Boys Girls Clubs 'It's always fun to try new sports,' 10th grader Lucas Phazekas said. 'I think it's pretty nice. I like it,' eighth grader Quinton Lynum said. During the first practice, Palm Beach Royals ambassadors were on the court helping coach the students. Quinton jumped on the court for his introductory lesson. 'It's pretty complicated, but the more you do it, the easier it is,' Lynum said. The ambassadors helped Lynum with technique and taught him the basics of the game. 'Well, they taught me how to hold a paddle, and when they taught me how to hold it, it kind of helped me. And when they taught me not to hit it so hard, it kind of helped me hit it more in bounds and get more points,' Lynum said. Lucas Phazekas said pickleball is like a mix of sports. 'Tennis, but if it was like ping pong,' Phazekas said. Phazekas said after one practice, he is starting to get the hang of it. 'I mean, I got it down somewhat at least,' Phazekas said. New paddles were also donated to the Boys Girls Clubs of Palm Beach County by Transworld Business Advisors. 'I hope the kids get to learn a new sport and get to be active and not be on their screens maybe for a few minutes and learning teamwork and learning new skills,' Andy Cagnetta said. 'We know the Boys and Girls Clubs are always worried about their budgets and where they're going to get equipment. And so we're happy as the business community to help that.' Terrance Johnson with the Boys Girls Clubs of Palm Beach County said the equipment will be put to good use, and any friendly activity to get students up and active is a huge benefit. 'It helps us save some money and keep some money in our pockets, and they can interact with the equipment for free. It's enough for multiple people to use at once,' Terrance Johnson said. After just one hour of playing pickleball, Lynum said all kids should give it a try. 'I think if you have anything on your mind, this is the type of thing that will kind of get things off your mind and have a lot of fun,' Lynum said.

entry.title: Celebrities tee off for a cause at Par for the Culture golf tournament in Greenacres
entry.summary: Golf, celebrities and community impact will come together on Monday, Oct. 19, as Par for the Culture celebrity golf tournament takes over Palm Beach National Golf Country Club, raising awareness and support for people experiencing homelessness in Palm Beach County. The event, organized by Darren Wingate, will bring together professional athletes, celebrities, influencers and community leaders for a day of golf with a purpose. WATCH BELOW: Golf tournament tees up support for The Lord's Place Par For the Culture Proceeds from the tournament will benefit The Lord's Place, a Palm Beach County nonprofit organization that provides housing assistance, supportive services and programs designed to help individuals and families experiencing homelessness rebuild their lives. For Wingate, the mission goes beyond the golf course. The tournament is designed to use the influence of sports and entertainment to bring attention to affordable housing, homelessness and the importance of community involvement. The event also aims to introduce new audiences to golf while creating opportunities for people from different backgrounds to connect through a shared cause. The Lord's Place works to address homelessness through services that include street outreach, housing support, employment training and programs that help people achieve greater independence. Organizers hope the tournament will encourage athletes and community leaders to use their platforms to support housing initiatives, not just in Palm Beach County, but in communities across the country. entry.article_text: The person shot during a shooting in Hobe Sound died Thursday, according to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office. The victim's mother identifies the shooting victim as Jarvis Preston, 21, of Hobe Sound. She says her son was shot by his best friend. She says she does not know what led to the shooting. She says Preston was not married, and he was the father of a small child. "It's just, it's dreadful, like, I can't, I can't understand what, why it expired to the way it did, because they, best friends. What escalated this to happen when it did?" said Ebony Preston, the mother of the shooting victim. The sheriff’s office began investigating the shooting Wednesday after it happened on Southeast Citrus Way, off Florida Avenue, in the Banner Lake neighborhood. Neighbors said they heard three gunshots around 8 p.m. Sheriff's Officials say Preston was armed with a handgun with a 30-clip magazine, which was recovered at the scene of the shooting Wednesday night. And they say Preston was shot and killed by his friend, who shot him from 10 feet away with an AR15 assault rifle. Now, what I gotta do, what? I gotta, like, it's horrible," Ebony Preston said. Preston's stepfather also wants answers. That's what I don't understand how it come about, 'cause they best friends," said Rodney Clemon, the victim's stepfather. Sheriff John Budensiek, Preston and his friend had been drinking earlier in the day, and Preston tried to rob his friend near their homes. "Multiple witnesses have now told us that he made threats to all kinds of people out on the street. He was yelling loudly, was extremely intoxicated, acting belligerent," Sheriff Budensiek said. The friend, who was armed with an AR15 assault rifle, came out of his house twice with his girlfriend. The second time, the friend and Jarvis Preston--who was armed with a handgun-- got into a confrontation that ended in gunfire. "The deceased (Preston) starts to pull out a handgun. Actually, it's a rifle, shoots him three times in the chest and he (Preston) drops right there," Sheriff Budensiek explained. Mary’s Medical Center in West Palm Beach and did not survive. Sheriff Budensiek says they have not determined yet if the shooting was self-defense or a murder. The victim's mother says it's devastating. "It's lot of unanswered questions. But my son is dead, so how do we go from there?" Ebony Preston said. See also: Funding for schools in Palm Beach County on your November ballot No one has been arrested. The Sheriff says they're working carefully with the State Attorney's Office to determine if anyone will be charged in this shooting or if it was a case of stand your ground, and if the shooter acted in self-defense. He says the individual who shot Preston attempted to render aid to the victim and remained at the scene following the shooting. The name of the shooter has not been released because the matter is still under investigation.

entry.title: Treasure Coast water tank in the running for a national award - WPBF
entry.summary: Treasure Coast water tank in the running for a national award    WPBF
entry.article_text: A water tank at Jaycee Park has been transformed into a colorful tribute to Florida’s native wildlife thanks to Stuart-born and raised artist Christian Stanley and his wife, Jessica. "We keep an eye on the happenings that are going on here in Fort Pierce and saw that there was an open call to artists and put together a design that we thought was a strong submission and submitted it, and we're fortunately selected to come out here and paint the tank," said Stanley, co-owner of C. The decades-old, 22-foot-tall tank that can hold a million gallons of water is owned by Fort Pierce Utilities Authority. It was once a bright shade of white; now it features colorful paintings of manatees, dolphins, turtles, fish and pelicans, along with a sunset. "The great joy that I get out of being of mural artist is taking stuff from the ocean, from the forest, whatever, and bringing it out to the streets for people to see in a much larger-than-life fashion," he said. "So, when I knew the call was interested in being kind of native Florida wildlife, I knew that we could really bring something together that would be really impactful for the community." On Tuesday, Stanley and his wife traveled from Central Florida to the Treasure Coast to apply a UV clear coat to help protect the artwork against the harsh environment of the shore. The two originally began painting the tank in August, completing the mural within a month. He said they then decided to enter their work into Tnemec Company, Inc.'s 2026 Tank of the Year, not expecting much. But became the only South Florida water tank in the running against dozens across the state and the country. "We're so excited," Stanley said.

entry.title: Young Stuart divers take a leap toward college scholarships, international competition and Olympic dreams
entry.summary: In life, they say, take a leap of faith. Well, a group of kids in Stuart are doing just that on a diving board. WATCH BELOW: Stuart divers take leap toward big dreams Stuart's Atlantic Diving Team teaches the Olympic sport of diving to kids of all ages,experience levels 'There are different things for different people. Some people prefer platform diving, which is much higher but fun, which I prefer. Something Ive grown to love is all the friendships that I make throughout the years,' said Grace Erickson, a local diver, who admits diving has always been her passion. 'On my preschool poster I wrote what I wanted to be when I got older was a diver,' Erickson said. That preschooler who could only dream of being a diver is fulfilling her dream as an eighth grader. 'Its been really exciting; it's new things every twist and turn, both in your head and diving off the board,' Erickson said. Her longtime coach, Osvaldo 'Pito' Alberty, thanks her for her courage and wants to see Erickson and her teammates take the sport to new levels. 'We are like a family here. We treat each other with respect and courtesy, and we push each other to do better than everyone else,' said Pito, whose passion is sharing his experience, knowledge and love for diving with young athletes with the Atlantic Diving Team in Stuart. Atlantic takes divers of all ages, backgrounds and experience levels and teaches them the Olympic sport of diving. 'The younger we get them, the better it is because over time they can get scholarships. If they want to do international diving, they can qualify for international competitions or even the Olympics,' Pito said. For divers like Erickson, she wants to take her talents to the college level, but there's a new diver whos just learning the sport, Carissa Smith. 'I was recently a gymnast and just about two months ago I started diving,' said Smith. Smith is a natural-born acrobat. At 14, she hasn't participated in her first competition because she wants to learn the basics. But for now, she admits diving is pretty fun. 'It feels like you're flying; it's exhilarating just being able to get better at my diving,' said Smith.

Something I’ve grown to love is all the friendships that I make throughout the years," said Grace Erickson, a local diver, who admits diving has always been her passion."On my preschool poster I wrote what I wanted to be when I got older was a diver," Erickson said.That preschooler who could only dream of being a diver is fulfilling her dream as an eighth grader."It’s been really exciting; it's new things every twist and turn, both in your head and diving off the board," Erickson said.Her longtime coach, Osvaldo "Pito" Alberty, thanks her for her courage and wants to see Erickson and her teammates take the sport to new levels."We are like a family here. We treat each other with respect and courtesy, and we push each other to do better than everyone else," said Pito, whose passion is sharing his experience, knowledge and love for diving with young athletes with the Atlantic Diving Team in Stuart.Atlantic takes divers of all ages, backgrounds and experience levels and teaches them the Olympic sport of diving."The younger we get them, the better it is because over time they can get scholarships. If they want to do international diving, they can qualify for international competitions or even the Olympics," Pito said.For divers like Erickson, she wants to take her talents to the college level, but there's a new diver who’s just learning the sport, Carissa Smith."I was recently a gymnast and just about two months ago I started diving," said Smith.Smith is a natural-born acrobat. At 14, she hasn't participated in her first competition because she wants to learn the basics. But for now, she admits diving is pretty fun."It feels like you're flying; it's exhilarating just being able to get better at my diving," said Smith.

entry.title: Prima Vista Boulevard safety plan in St. Lucie County would add raised median after 578 crashes since 2020
entry.summary: WPTV is learning that potential road improvements are coming to a busy road in Port St. Lucie. St. Lucie County staff are sharing designs and want to hear input from neighbors about a proposed project on Prima Vista Boulevard. WATCH BELOW: Neighbors weigh in on Prima Vista Boulevard changes St. Lucie County wants input on improvements to this busy road They plan to improve a section of the roadway from Airoso Boulevard to U.S. Highway 1 by removing the center left turn lanes Dan Zrallack, county engineer, said their plan is to replace the center left-turn lanes with a raised median. 'The center turn lane is often referred to as a suicide lane,' Zrallack said. 'The more turning movements you have, the more chances you have for accidents by restricting access and putting in the median turn lanes. We can kind of control where those turning movements are and protect the drivers as well as pedestrians walking along the roadway.'  According to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, there have been 578 crashes on that section of the Prima Vista Boulevard since 2020.  Zrallack said the median will make the road safer.  'Statistically, the safety improves by up to like 40 percent or more,' Zrallack said.  But not every neighbor is sold on the improvements.  Kadaysha Wilkins lives on Prima Vista Boulevard and told WPTV the median will make traveling more complicated.  'Adding medians or anything else is going to cause more chaos than good,' Wilkins said. 'Ten to 12 years of living here, I've never seen an issue with our turning lane.'  Wilkins said it'll make it more difficult to take her niece and nephew to school by using the median instead of driving across the street.  'A five-minute ride has turned into a 15-minute travel,' Wilkins said. Wilkins said trying to come home could also be an issue. 'Turning into my driveway, which could have taken two seconds, is that now going to take 15 minutes? Wilkins said.   Zrallack said he hears the concerns and hopes they can address them on Thursday night during their public meeting. 'We're hoping to get more of that by hearing from the community again and seeing what else we can do to refine the design,' Zrallack said. A second in-person public meeting for the project was held Thursday at the MidFlorida Credit Union Event Center.

entry.title: How to find your polling place in Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast
entry.summary: Before heading to the polls for Florida's 2026 general election, voters should confirm where they are assigned to vote. Polling places can change between election cycles, and election officials recommend checking your polling location well before Election Day. Voters in Palm Beach County, St. Lucie County, Martin County, Indian River County and Okeechobee County can visit their local supervisor of elections website to verify registration information, view their sample ballot and locate their assigned polling place. How do I find my polling place? Most county election offices offer online voter lookup tools that allow voters to: Verify voter registration status View a sample ballot Find their precinct Locate their Election Day polling site Confirm district assignments Can I vote at any polling place? On Election Day, voters must generally cast a ballot at their assigned polling location. During early voting, voters may use any authorized early voting location within their county. What should I bring? Voters should bring a valid photo ID with a signature. Those who arrive without acceptable identification may be eligible to cast a provisional ballot.

entry.title: AmeriCorps returns to Martin County with renewed focus on boosting students' reading skills - WFLX
entry.summary: AmeriCorps returns to Martin County with renewed focus on boosting students' reading skills    WFLX
entry.article_text: A program that has worked with thousands of Martin County children is returning after a brief hiatus, with a renewed focus on helping young students strengthen their reading skills. The Boys Girls Clubs of Martin County is celebrating the return of its AmeriCorps program, which places volunteers directly with students to provide individualized and small-group academic support. WATCH BELOW: Literacy program returns to Martin County after hiatus “We missed it. It was an extremely important piece to our success and moving the district forward,” Martin County Schools Superintendent Michael Maine said. The Boys Girls Clubs of Martin County first introduced the federal mentorship program to the area in 2019. For six years, AmeriCorps volunteers worked with thousands of local students before federal funding shortfalls forced the program to pause. Now, program leaders have set new goals for its return. WPTV reporter Christy Waite connected with AmeriCorps Program Director for Martin County Boys and Girls Club, Russell Lamberti. “We want to serve 575 students, and we want to see an increase of 65% growth, and that can be in vocabulary, fluency and grammar,” AmeriCorps Program Director Russell Lamberti said. AmeriCorps volunteers will work one-on-one and in small groups with kindergarten through fifth-grade students at four Boys Girls Club locations, with an emphasis on literacy. For AmeriCorps Volunteer Experience Specialist Abelard Cesar, the mission also has a personal connection. I learned English at 13 years old, and I had mentors that helped me grow,” Cesar said. The Boys Girls Clubs says the program delivered significant academic results during its previous six-year run. In some cases, as many as eight in 10 participating students moved their reading from Level 1 to Level 4. About the same percentage maintained or improved their English Language Arts grades, according to the organization. The organization said students also showed improvements in literacy rates, assessment scores, school attendance and behavioral patterns. AmeriCorps members’ work previously extended beyond the classroom. According to the Boys Girls Clubs, volunteers completed nearly 50 service projects in Martin County and contributed more than 60,000 hours to community cleanup efforts and other acts of service. The return comes as literacy remains a focus across the county. Earlier this year, the Martin County School District reported that local kindergarten students tied for fourth place statewide in readiness scores and literacy assessments. The AmeriCorps program is part of a broader academic effort by the Boys Girls Clubs of Martin County, which serves more than 1,000 members ages 6 to 18 in its daily programs. The organization also provides after-school academic assistance through certified teachers. Beyond its Clubs, the organization runs or manages several programs serving local children, including Reading Buddies, Character Counts!, career training using virtual reality technology, culinary programs and skilled-trades programs. With AmeriCorps volunteers returning, the Boys Girls Clubs says it hopes to build on the program’s previous results while giving more Martin County students the individual attention and support they need.

entry.title: Martin County deputies investigate whether fatal Hobe Sound shooting was Stand Your Ground
entry.summary: A 21-year-old man was fatally shot by a man investigators say was his friend on SE Citrus Way in the Banner Lake neighborhood of Hobe Sound. The Martin County Sheriff's Office is now working to determine whether the shooting qualifies as a Stand Your Ground case. The victim has been identified as Jarvis Preston. No one has been arrested. The Martin County Sheriff is still weighing whether the facts point to a homicide charge or a Stand Your Ground defense. WATCH BELOW: Shooting investigated as possible Stand Your Ground case Martin County Sheriff's Office investigates deadly Hobe Sound shooting among friends The sheriff's office says the two men had been drinking together Wednesday afternoon. Detectives believe Preston continued to drink into the evening, then attempted to rob his friend, who investigators have not publicly identified. The friend got away, but investigators say Preston followed him home and threatened him. 'The deceased starts to pull out a handgun. Shooter pulls out his AR-15 rifle, shoots him three times in the chest, and he drops right there,' John Budensiek of the Martin County Sheriff's Office said. After the shooting, Preston's friend allegedly dropped his weapon, unarmed Preston, and started to render aid until deputies arrived. Investigators are searching for surveillance video and speaking with several witnesses to determine whether Florida's Stand Your Ground law applies. 'We're really not ready to make that determination. But I want to make sure we do it the right way to send the right messages to the right people, so this doesn't happen again,' Budensiek said. The shooting has shaken the tight-knit Banner Lake community. Neighbor Stephanie Rose described the loss. 'It's just sad, really sad,' Stephanie Rose said. Rose said she knew both men. 'They were good kids, I mean, they got along perfectly. ... They were friends. I don't know what happened,' Rose said. As Preston's family and neighbors grieve, the community is coming to terms with the loss of a young life. 'Unbelievable, and it's just sad. I was just on my way to give them my condolences,' Rose said. This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: Drinking, threats and guns: New information released in fatal shooting of 21-year-old in Hobe Sound - WPBF
entry.summary: Drinking, threats and guns: New information released in fatal shooting of 21-year-old in Hobe Sound    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 21-year-old man was fatally shot Wednesday night in the Banner Lake neighborhood of Hobe Sound, and authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident. Martin County sheriff's deputies responded to the scene along Southeast Citrus Way, where they found Jarvis Preston with three gunshot wounds to the chest. "I know you're going to ask me, was it a stand your ground? And the answer is, I don't know right now," Sheriff John Budensiek said. Budensiek explained that Preston and the shooter were friends. Witnesses reported that Preston had been drinking heavily throughout the day and began threatening the shooter and others while armed with a gun. "He's talking, I'm going to shoot you, I'm going to hurt you. The shooter walks towards him, now they're at the edge of the road, at which point the deceased starts to pull out a handgun. The shooter pulls out his AR-15, actually it's a rifle, shoots him three times in the chest, and he drops right there," Budensiek said. The sheriff said the shooter called 911 and attempted life-saving efforts before Preston was flown to St. Mary’s Hospital, where he died. Preston’s grandmother, Harriet Ford Gregg, said she heard the gunshots and later saw her grandson lying on the ground. "It was Jarvis laying on the ground out there, and the police officer was reviving him," Gregg said. She shared her grief over losing Preston, who lived with her, saying his empty bedroom is now too painful to face. I'm not going in there," Gregg said. entry.title: Avelo Airlines announces nonstop flights from West Palm Beach to North Dallas area
entry.summary: Avelo Airlines is adding a new nonstop route connecting West Palm Beach with the North Dallas area beginning in December. The airline announced Thursday that it will begin nonstop service between President Donald J. Trump International Airport (DJT) and North Dallas/McKinney National Airport (DTX) on Dec. 17. WATCH BELOW: New nonstop flights announced from DJT to North Texas Avelo announces nonstop flights from West Palm Beach to North Dallas Flights will operate twice a week, on Thursdays and Sundays. Avelo says it will be the only airline offering nonstop service between the two airports. Introductory one-way fares start at $69, according to the airline. The new route will give Palm Beach County travelers another option for reaching the Dallas area. McKinney National Airport is located north of Dallas and is promoted as an alternative to the region's larger airports. With the addition of McKinney, Avelo will serve three nonstop destinations from DJT. The airline also offers service to Tweed-New Haven Airport in Connecticut and Wilmington Airport, which serves the Philadelphia and Delaware Valley region. 'Were excited to bring a new nonstop route to the Palm Beaches and make it easier than ever for travelers to connect between South Florida and North Dallas/McKinney,' Avelo Airlines founder and CEO Andrew Levy said in the release. Reservations are available through Avelo Airlines .

entry.summary: 1 person dies after shooting in Hobe Sound, no arrest made    WPEC
entry.article_text: The person shot during a shooting in Hobe Sound died Thursday, according to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office. The victim's mother identifies the shooting victim as Jarvis Preston, 21, of Hobe Sound. She says her son was shot by his best friend. She says she does not know what led to the shooting. She says Preston was not married, and he was the father of a small child. "It's just, it's dreadful, like, I can't, I can't understand what, why it expired to the way it did, because they, best friends. What escalated this to happen when it did?" said Ebony Preston, the mother of the shooting victim. The sheriff’s office began investigating the shooting Wednesday after it happened on Southeast Citrus Way, off Florida Avenue, in the Banner Lake neighborhood. Neighbors said they heard three gunshots around 8 p.m. Sheriff's Officials say Preston was armed with a handgun with a 30-clip magazine, which was recovered at the scene of the shooting Wednesday night. And they say Preston was shot and killed by his friend, who shot him from 10 feet away with an AR15 assault rifle. Now, what I gotta do, what? I gotta, like, it's horrible," Ebony Preston said. Preston's stepfather also wants answers. That's what I don't understand how it come about, 'cause they best friends," said Rodney Clemon, the victim's stepfather. Sheriff John Budensiek, Preston and his friend had been drinking earlier in the day, and Preston tried to rob his friend near their homes. "Multiple witnesses have now told us that he made threats to all kinds of people out on the street. He was yelling loudly, was extremely intoxicated, acting belligerent," Sheriff Budensiek said. The friend, who was armed with an AR15 assault rifle, came out of his house twice with his girlfriend. The second time, the friend and Jarvis Preston--who was armed with a handgun-- got into a confrontation that ended in gunfire. "The deceased (Preston) starts to pull out a handgun. Actually, it's a rifle, shoots him three times in the chest and he (Preston) drops right there," Sheriff Budensiek explained. Mary’s Medical Center in West Palm Beach and did not survive. Sheriff Budensiek says they have not determined yet if the shooting was self-defense or a murder. The victim's mother says it's devastating. "It's lot of unanswered questions. But my son is dead, so how do we go from there?" Ebony Preston said. See also: Funding for schools in Palm Beach County on your November ballot No one has been arrested. The Sheriff says they're working carefully with the State Attorney's Office to determine if anyone will be charged in this shooting or if it was a case of stand your ground, and if the shooter acted in self-defense. He says the individual who shot Preston attempted to render aid to the victim and remained at the scene following the shooting. The name of the shooter has not been released because the matter is still under investigation.

entry.summary: Two kittens rescued after being buried alive in Hobe Sound are recovering in foster care and showing signs of remarkable progress just days after investigators say they survived a tragic act of animal cruelty. Kali and Amara, two approximately 4-week-old kittens, are now living with a Treasure Coast family after Martin County Sheriff's Office deputies rescued them from the ground last week. Authorities say 36-year-old Alba Chavez buried multiple kittens alive because she believed they were demons. The case has drawn widespread attention across the Treasure Coast, where animal advocates and residents have followed the kittens' recovery. As the community processes the disturbing allegations, Kali and Amara's survival has become a symbol of resilience and hope. Rescued Hobe Sound kittens recover with foster family after being buried alive Deputies rescued two kittens buried alive Body camera video released by the Martin County Sheriff's Office shows deputies digging to reach the kittens after receiving reports about the incident. Video captured one deputy expressing surprise that the animals were still alive as rescue efforts unfolded. entry.article_text: A welfare check on an 88-year-old Okeechobee County veteran led to the discovery of a homicide and the arrest of the victim's grandson following an early-morning police chase in Indian River County, Sheriff Eric Flowers and Chief Deputy Michael Hazellief said Thursday during a press conference.WATCH BELOW: Sheriffs announce arrest of wanted suspectPaul Eugene Baker, a longtime Okeechobee County resident and veteran, was found dead on his property after his daughter-in-law called for a welfare check. His grandson, 35-year-old Earl Douglas Wadlington III, was taken into custody after deputies pursued him through a Walmart parking lot at approximately 4 a.m."What started off as a simple welfare check of an 88-year-old veteran in our county has turned into a tragedy and a family tragedy," Hazellief said.Baker's daughter-in-law had not seen or heard from him in several days. She went to his residence and found the house in disarray, which investigators said was highly unusual."She hadn't seen him or talked to him in several days. She went by to check on the residence. She found the house in disarray, became concerned, and it was highly unusual for him to not be around or for the house to be in this manner," Hazellief said.Law enforcement obtained and executed a search warrant for the property. Baker was found dead on the property. Investigators said the manner and location of his death made it immediately evident that it was a homicide.Baker's only vehicle was also missing from the residence, along with other property. Investigators learned that Wadlington had recently been living with Baker.The daughter-in-law told investigators that Wadlington had a history with the criminal justice system and that no other family member would allow him to live with them. Wadlington has over 800 felonies in his criminal background, the chief deputy said."The daughter-in-law also explained to us that he had been in and out of prison, that he had challenges that nobody else in the family would allow him to live with him, but the grandfather had allowed him to stay there," Hazellief said.Because the daughter-in-law also held power of attorney for Baker, law enforcement was able to enter the missing vehicle into the ALPR system — a license plate reader network connected to partner agencies across the Treasure Coast area — as stolen. The vehicle was flagged as connected to a homicide suspect. Investigators tracked the vehicle leaving the area but chose not to issue a public alert."We didn't put anything out publicly at that time because we did not want to startle. We wanted the suspect to stay in the vehicle. Quite honestly, we wanted to keep driving," Hazellief said.WATCH BELOW: Dashcam video of chase, bodycam video of arrest in Indian River CountyInvestigators noted that while the agency was required this past month to remove Flock cameras from state roads and permitted locations per a state DOT order, cameras in other qualifying locations remained operational and allowed investigators to move forward with the case."To be specific with the language, we still have them in place in places that don't meet that criteria, and because of that, we were able to really move forward with this case," Hazellief said.Senior detective Ashley Rojas and her team led the investigation, the chief deputy said.The stolen vehicle was detected by Indian River County's Flock camera system this morning, leading investigators to the suspect's location.Indian River County Sheriff Flowers described the early-morning pursuit caught on video, in which Wadlington fled from deputies through a Walmart parking lot."One of the particular things that's interesting is it's 4 o'clock in the morning. He's running from our deputies. He's running through the Walmart parking lot. You see that our deputies were able to deploy stop sticks. The reason that he ultimately stopped and got out and ran is because his truck was going to stop working. That stolen vehicle is going to stop working," Flowers said.Sebastian Police Department also responded and assisted Indian River County deputies throughout the pursuit."Doesn't matter if the uniform is green or blue, doesn't matter what color it is. We're all going to go after the bad guys," Flowers said.Flowers praised the Flock camera system and said the county will continue using it despite public criticism."For all the naysayers and all the people who don't like flock and who don't like it, we're going to continue to use it. We're going to continue to put bad guys in jail because of it," Flowers said.Flowers noted that Indian River County cameras not covered by the state DOT order remain in operation. He said the Flock system has aided in other cases, including one involving a missing elderly woman.Wadlington was arrested on fleeing and eluding charges, deputies said, in addition to driving a stolen a vehicle. Both agencies said they are working very closely with the state attorney's office to obtain a warrant for his arrest for the homicide very soon."This guy is the definition of somebody who needs to stay behind bars," Flowers said.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.summary: 1 person dies after shooting in Hobe Sound, no arrest made    WPEC
entry.article_text: The person shot during a shooting in Hobe Sound died Thursday, according to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office. The victim's mother identifies the shooting victim as Jarvis Preston, 21, of Hobe Sound. She says her son was shot by his best friend. She says she does not know what led to the shooting. She says Preston was not married, and he was the father of a small child. "It's just, it's dreadful, like, I can't, I can't understand what, why it expired to the way it did, because they, best friends. What escalated this to happen when it did?" said Ebony Preston, the mother of the shooting victim. The sheriff’s office began investigating the shooting Wednesday after it happened on Southeast Citrus Way, off Florida Avenue, in the Banner Lake neighborhood. Neighbors said they heard three gunshots around 8 p.m. Sheriff's Officials say Preston was armed with a handgun with a 30-clip magazine, which was recovered at the scene of the shooting Wednesday night. And they say Preston was shot and killed by his friend, who shot him from 10 feet away with an AR15 assault rifle. Now, what I gotta do, what? I gotta, like, it's horrible," Ebony Preston said. Preston's stepfather also wants answers. That's what I don't understand how it come about, 'cause they best friends," said Rodney Clemon, the victim's stepfather. Sheriff John Budensiek, Preston and his friend had been drinking earlier in the day, and Preston tried to rob his friend near their homes. "Multiple witnesses have now told us that he made threats to all kinds of people out on the street. He was yelling loudly, was extremely intoxicated, acting belligerent," Sheriff Budensiek said. The friend, who was armed with an AR15 assault rifle, came out of his house twice with his girlfriend. The second time, the friend and Jarvis Preston--who was armed with a handgun-- got into a confrontation that ended in gunfire. "The deceased (Preston) starts to pull out a handgun. Actually, it's a rifle, shoots him three times in the chest and he (Preston) drops right there," Sheriff Budensiek explained. Mary’s Medical Center in West Palm Beach and did not survive. Sheriff Budensiek says they have not determined yet if the shooting was self-defense or a murder. The victim's mother says it's devastating. "It's lot of unanswered questions. But my son is dead, so how do we go from there?" Ebony Preston said. See also: Funding for schools in Palm Beach County on your November ballot No one has been arrested. The Sheriff says they're working carefully with the State Attorney's Office to determine if anyone will be charged in this shooting or if it was a case of stand your ground, and if the shooter acted in self-defense. He says the individual who shot Preston attempted to render aid to the victim and remained at the scene following the shooting. The name of the shooter has not been released because the matter is still under investigation.

entry.summary: Drinking, threats and guns: New information released in fatal shooting of 21-year-old in Hobe Sound    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 21-year-old man was fatally shot Wednesday night in the Banner Lake neighborhood of Hobe Sound, and authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident. Martin County sheriff's deputies responded to the scene along Southeast Citrus Way, where they found Jarvis Preston with three gunshot wounds to the chest. "I know you're going to ask me, was it a stand your ground? And the answer is, I don't know right now," Sheriff John Budensiek said. Budensiek explained that Preston and the shooter were friends. Witnesses reported that Preston had been drinking heavily throughout the day and began threatening the shooter and others while armed with a gun. "He's talking, I'm going to shoot you, I'm going to hurt you. The shooter walks towards him, now they're at the edge of the road, at which point the deceased starts to pull out a handgun. The shooter pulls out his AR-15, actually it's a rifle, shoots him three times in the chest, and he drops right there," Budensiek said. The sheriff said the shooter called 911 and attempted life-saving efforts before Preston was flown to St. Mary’s Hospital, where he died. Preston’s grandmother, Harriet Ford Gregg, said she heard the gunshots and later saw her grandson lying on the ground. "It was Jarvis laying on the ground out there, and the police officer was reviving him," Gregg said. She shared her grief over losing Preston, who lived with her, saying his empty bedroom is now too painful to face. I'm not going in there," Gregg said. entry.article_text: A shooting in the Banner Lake area of Hobe Sound on Wednesday night left one person dead, according to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office. Deputies responded to the scene along Southeast Citrus Way and spent hours investigating. Authorities said one person was detained for questioning. Harriet Ford Greg, who said the victim was her grandson, shared that he lived with her. She recalled hearing three gunshots while she was in bed and immediately worrying about him, knowing he was out that night. When she stepped outside, she said she saw him on the ground as first responders tried to save him. " laying on the ground out there and the police officer was reviving him," Greg said. "I thought that he's not going to make it. Somebody shot him." Greg said she is trying to stay strong for her family but admitted she cannot bring herself to walk into the room where her grandson stayed, saying none of this feels real. The proposal focuses on the stretch between Aroso Boulevard and U.S. It would replace the center turn lane with a raised median and add landscaping designed to make the road feel narrower and encourage drivers to slow down. County officials say the changes are intended to improve safety, reduce crashes, and help slow traffic along the corridor. A majority of the community members spoke out against the plan, saying they don't believe the changes would improve safety. County leaders said feedback from the meeting will help shape the project. Otto Lenke was found guilty in May of shooting and killing Richard Benson inside the victim's bike shop, Fast Frank's , back in February 2021. Prosecutors showed the jury surveillance video of the crime during the trial back in May. entry.title: AmeriCorps returns to Martin County with renewed focus on boosting students' reading skills - WFLX
entry.summary: AmeriCorps returns to Martin County with renewed focus on boosting students' reading skills    WFLX
entry.article_text: A program that has worked with thousands of Martin County children is returning after a brief hiatus, with a renewed focus on helping young students strengthen their reading skills. The Boys Girls Clubs of Martin County is celebrating the return of its AmeriCorps program, which places volunteers directly with students to provide individualized and small-group academic support. WATCH BELOW: Literacy program returns to Martin County after hiatus “We missed it. It was an extremely important piece to our success and moving the district forward,” Martin County Schools Superintendent Michael Maine said. The Boys Girls Clubs of Martin County first introduced the federal mentorship program to the area in 2019. For six years, AmeriCorps volunteers worked with thousands of local students before federal funding shortfalls forced the program to pause. Now, program leaders have set new goals for its return. WPTV reporter Christy Waite connected with AmeriCorps Program Director for Martin County Boys and Girls Club, Russell Lamberti. “We want to serve 575 students, and we want to see an increase of 65% growth, and that can be in vocabulary, fluency and grammar,” AmeriCorps Program Director Russell Lamberti said. AmeriCorps volunteers will work one-on-one and in small groups with kindergarten through fifth-grade students at four Boys Girls Club locations, with an emphasis on literacy. For AmeriCorps Volunteer Experience Specialist Abelard Cesar, the mission also has a personal connection. I learned English at 13 years old, and I had mentors that helped me grow,” Cesar said. The Boys Girls Clubs says the program delivered significant academic results during its previous six-year run. In some cases, as many as eight in 10 participating students moved their reading from Level 1 to Level 4. About the same percentage maintained or improved their English Language Arts grades, according to the organization. The organization said students also showed improvements in literacy rates, assessment scores, school attendance and behavioral patterns. AmeriCorps members’ work previously extended beyond the classroom. According to the Boys Girls Clubs, volunteers completed nearly 50 service projects in Martin County and contributed more than 60,000 hours to community cleanup efforts and other acts of service. The return comes as literacy remains a focus across the county. Earlier this year, the Martin County School District reported that local kindergarten students tied for fourth place statewide in readiness scores and literacy assessments. The AmeriCorps program is part of a broader academic effort by the Boys Girls Clubs of Martin County, which serves more than 1,000 members ages 6 to 18 in its daily programs. The organization also provides after-school academic assistance through certified teachers. Beyond its Clubs, the organization runs or manages several programs serving local children, including Reading Buddies, Character Counts!, career training using virtual reality technology, culinary programs and skilled-trades programs. With AmeriCorps volunteers returning, the Boys Girls Clubs says it hopes to build on the program’s previous results while giving more Martin County students the individual attention and support they need.

entry.title: Suspected fentanyl trafficker arrested after 115 mph chase on I-95 in St. Lucie County - WPBF
entry.summary: Suspected fentanyl trafficker arrested after 115 mph chase on I-95 in St. Lucie County    WPBF
entry.article_text: A suspected fentanyl trafficker is behind bars after investigators say he sold drugs to a person who later died of an overdose, then led law enforcement on a high-speed chase that reached 115 mph and ended in Martin County. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro identified the suspect as 43-year-old James Arthur Green, who he said is a 10-time convicted felon. According to the sheriff, the investigation began after a fatal fentanyl overdose on Oct. Detectives used the victim’s phone to contact Green, who allegedly returned to the victim’s home Tuesday to deliver more fentanyl. Investigators say Green even sent a picture to the victim’s phone showing where he had left the drugs, unaware that he had been communicating with law enforcement the entire time. "Obviously, he didn’t know that this person had passed away. We were communicating with them," Del Toro said. Later that day, investigators say Green attempted to sell more fentanyl during an undercover operation. When detectives moved in to arrest him, Green fled, striking an unmarked St. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office cruiser before leading law enforcement on a pursuit down Interstate 95. Authorities say the chase reached speeds of 115 mph and continued into Martin County. The pursuit eventually ended near Kanner Highway after Florida Highway Patrol troopers deployed stop sticks and performed a PIT maneuver to stop Green’s vehicle. Del Toro emphasized the dangers of fentanyl and the importance of removing suspected traffickers from the community. This is killing our citizens and our community and preying upon people that have substance abuse problems," Del Toro said. "So I’m very, very happy this person’s off the streets right now." Green now faces multiple drug-related charges, along with additional charges connected to the pursuit. He is being held on a $440,000 bond. entry.article_text: Three seniors at Alexander W. Dreyfoos School of the Arts have created Prodigy Pro, a free artificial intelligence platform designed to help students turn their ideas into real-world ventures.Co-founders Aiden Azoy and Anthony Tan and Head of Design Mia Rubio developed the platform after attending South Florida business networking events and realizing how few students were in the room.WATCH: Dreyfoos seniors build free AI platform for student entrepreneurs“We attended networking events and we noticed, why are we the youngest people in the room?” Azoy said. “There are so many talented students in our communities where they’re able to pursue their professional careers outside of school.”The students said they wanted to give young people a way to explore their interests, develop practical ideas and participate in West Palm Beach’s growing business community.The founders attend Dreyfoos in downtown West Palm Beach, where new development and the arrival of major companies have fueled the area’s growing reputation as “Wall Street South.”“We go to Dreyfoos, and literally hundreds of feet away are these huge constructions of Related Ross, companies like ServiceNow or even Citadel moving down to South Florida,” Tan said. “We’re right at the forefront of this new business center that is becoming West Palm Beach.”Tan said the students attempted to connect with professionals at local gatherings but struggled to find opportunities intended for people their age.“We tried to go to these meetings, and a lot of the time there wouldn’t be any opportunity for us,” Tan said. “So that’s why we wanted to create our own.”Prodigy Pro was built to help students take the first steps toward developing projects and businesses.“Prodigy Pro is a free AI entrepreneurship platform that helps a student take their idea from an idea to the final product,” Tan said.Azoy said the team created the platform after noticing that many students were not taking their ideas beyond the classroom.“Prodigy Pro is a way for students to build real ventures outside of school and be able to pursue their professional interests,” Azoy said. “We noticed that not enough students are getting out there and really putting their ideas out into the world. We gave them the ability to do that.”Users enter information about an idea and the problem they hope to solve. The platform’s AI then helps organize the concept and identify potential next steps.Rubio designed the user interface and worked to make the process understandable for students who may have little or no previous business experience.“You upload your information and the idea that you really want to pursue,” Rubio said. “And the AI will help you guide and shape and really tell you what your next step is, as well as create roadmaps, reminders and just really help your venture get off the ground.”The platform divides the development process into smaller sections and tasks.“With Prodigy [Pro], we wanted to make the next step super easy and attainable,” Rubio said. “So we grouped things into different sections and made each task super easy for the user to understand, so they know what to do next with their venture.”During a demonstration, the students used concerns about a school bus route to show how a user could enter a problem and explore possible efficiencies. “You input your information, and it really gives you the next steps, what you should do, and you can ask the AI to help develop your venture,” Rubio said.The founders said making Prodigy Pro free was central to their mission. Azoy said students should have access to the same entrepreneurial tools regardless of their school or community’s resources.“It’s completely free for students, and we want to stress that because we want to basically give the message that a student in an underprivileged school or community should have the same exact resources as, you know, a student in a resourced school,” Azoy said.According to the students, Prodigy Pro has grown to more than 15,000 users in 20 countries.The team also competed in the Mott Million Dollar Challenge, a national student entrepreneurship competition.“A few months ago in May, we competed in the Mott Million Dollar Challenge, where we won $7,500 for our venture,” Tan said.Tan said the prize money was reinvested into Prodigy Pro.“A lot of it went into the development of the platform, going through the UI, the back end, also enabling the AI to be free for other students,” he said.The three founders are seniors preparing for life after high school, but they said Prodigy Pro will continue.Asked whether the platform would remain after graduation, Rubio responded, “Yes, of course. It’ll remain to be a free platform for our users.”For Azoy, the larger goal is to show young people that they do not have to wait to begin developing their professional interests.“We really think that it’s important for them to be showing up and, you know, building ventures that really matter because every student has creativity in an underprivileged or privileged school,” Azoy said.The students’ work comes as artificial intelligence becomes increasingly integrated into education, business and everyday problem-solving. By making the platform free, the Dreyfoos seniors hope more young people will be able to turn their creativity into action and create opportunities of their own.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.article_text: A water tank at Jaycee Park has been transformed into a colorful tribute to Florida’s native wildlife thanks to Stuart-born and raised artist Christian Stanley and his wife, Jessica. "We keep an eye on the happenings that are going on here in Fort Pierce and saw that there was an open call to artists and put together a design that we thought was a strong submission and submitted it, and we're fortunately selected to come out here and paint the tank," said Stanley, co-owner of C. The decades-old, 22-foot-tall tank that can hold a million gallons of water is owned by Fort Pierce Utilities Authority. It was once a bright shade of white; now it features colorful paintings of manatees, dolphins, turtles, fish and pelicans, along with a sunset. "The great joy that I get out of being of mural artist is taking stuff from the ocean, from the forest, whatever, and bringing it out to the streets for people to see in a much larger-than-life fashion," he said. "So, when I knew the call was interested in being kind of native Florida wildlife, I knew that we could really bring something together that would be really impactful for the community." On Tuesday, Stanley and his wife traveled from Central Florida to the Treasure Coast to apply a UV clear coat to help protect the artwork against the harsh environment of the shore. The two originally began painting the tank in August, completing the mural within a month. He said they then decided to enter their work into Tnemec Company, Inc.'s 2026 Tank of the Year, not expecting much. But became the only South Florida water tank in the running against dozens across the state and the country. "We're so excited," Stanley said.

The sheriff said the shooter called 911 and attempted life-saving efforts before Preston was flown to St. Mary’s Hospital, where he died. Preston’s grandmother, Harriet Ford Gregg, said she heard the gunshots and later saw her grandson lying on the ground. "It was Jarvis laying on the ground out there, and the police officer was reviving him," Gregg said. entry.title: Investigators question if fatal shooting in Hobe Sound falls under stand-your-ground law - WPBF
entry.summary: Investigators question if fatal shooting in Hobe Sound falls under stand-your-ground law    WPBF
entry.article_text: Investigators in Martin County are working to determine whether a fatal shooting in the Banner Lake neighborhood of Hobe Sound was a crime or if the shooter acted within Florida's stand-your-ground law. The Martin County Sheriff’s Office said the shooter told them he and his friend were on Southeast Citrus Way on Wednesday night when an argument escalated. According to the shooter, his friend repeatedly threatened to shoot him and even showed him a gun. "The deceased starts to pull out a handgun. The shooter pulls out his AR-15, actually, it's a rifle, shoots him three times in the chest, and he drops right there," Sheriff John Budensiek said. Family members identified the deceased as Jarvis Preston. The sheriff’s office has not released the identity of the shooter. "I know you're going to ask me, was it a stand-your-ground? And the answer is, I don't know right now," Budensiek said. Dave Aronberg, the former Palm Beach County state attorney who is not involved in this case but has experience with stand-your-ground cases, said the shooter’s account suggests it could fall under the law. "The shooter must have reasonably believed that firing the weapon was immediately necessary to prevent imminent death or great bodily harm," Aronberg said. However, Aronberg noted that if Preston did not pull a gun, never had a gun, or if the shooter was the aggressor, the stand your ground defense would not apply. "You can't start a fight, provoke the confrontation and then shoot your way out of it," Aronberg said. The sheriff said investigators are still working to locate and interview witnesses to the shooting. entry.article_text: A 21-year-old man was fatally shot by a man investigators say was his friend on SE Citrus Way in the Banner Lake neighborhood of Hobe Sound. The Martin County Sheriff's Office is now working to determine whether the shooting qualifies as a Stand Your Ground case.The victim has been identified as Jarvis Preston. The Martin County Sheriff is still weighing whether the facts point to a homicide charge or a Stand Your Ground defense.The sheriff's office says the two men had been drinking together Wednesday afternoon. Detectives believe Preston continued to drink into the evening, then attempted to rob his friend, who investigators have not publicly identified. The friend got away, but investigators say Preston followed him home and threatened him."The deceased starts to pull out a handgun. Shooter pulls his AR-15, acts a rifle, shoots him three times in the chest, and he drops right there," John Budensiek of the Martin County Sheriff's Office said.After the shooting, Preston’s friend allegedly dropped his weapon, unarmed Preston, and started to render aid until deputies arrived.Investigators are searching for surveillance video and speaking with several witnesses to determine whether Florida's Stand Your Ground law applies."We're really not ready to make that determination. But I want to make sure we do it the right way to send the right messages to the right people, so this doesn't happen again," Budensiek said.The shooting has shaken the tight-knit Banner Lake community. Neighbor Stephanie Rose described the loss."It's just sad, really sad," Stephanie Rose said.Rose said she knew both men."They were good kids, I mean they got a long perfect, I mean they were friends. I don't know what happened," Rose said.As Preston's family and neighbors grieve, the community is coming to terms with the loss of a young life."Unbelievable and it's just sad. entry.title: Woman charged with animal cruelty after bringing 'severely emaciated' dog to veterinarian
entry.summary: A West Palm Beach woman is facing a felony animal cruelty charge after investigators said her Yorkshire terrier was so severely malnourished that veterinarians gave the dog the lowest possible body condition score before it was euthanized. The investigation began Oct. 2 when Palm Beach County Animal Care and Control officers responded to Access Specialty Animal Hospital in Royal Palm Beach after staff reported a suspected animal cruelty case involving a 7-year-old Yorkshire terrier named King. Veterinary staff told investigators King arrived in critical condition suffering from severe emaciation, a heavy flea infestation and signs of prolonged neglect. According to the affidavit, veterinarians assigned King a 1 out of 9 body condition score on the Purina Body Condition Scale, the lowest possible rating, indicating extreme emaciation. The attending veterinarian told investigators the dog was non-responsive, severely hypothermic and in respiratory and cardiac distress when he arrived. According to the affidavit, the Yorkie was unable to breathe on his own. The veterinarian determined King's condition was the result of a chronic deterioration that developed over weeks or months rather than a sudden illness. Despite emergency lifesaving measures, including intubation and assisted ventilation, the dog's condition remained poor due to the severity of his condition. The veterinarian said the dog's emaciation as among the most severe she had encountered in her veterinary career and concluded King's suffering was most likely caused by prolonged neglect and a lack of adequate care. The affidavit states Marseille and another individual declined an advanced stabilization treatment recommended by the hospital because they could not afford the cost. Hospital staff identified Charlynn Marseille, 33, as the person who brought King to the veterinary hospital. Investigators later confirmed ownership through animal records and an interview at Marseille's West Palm Beach residence, where she acknowledged owning the dog. Investigators also referenced a 2023 complaint involving the same dog. According to the affidavit, a caller reported concerns that King had been left alone for days without food and was crying. Marseille was arrested Oct. 14 and charged with aggravated animal cruelty causing excessive pain or suffering. She is being held at the Palm Beach County

entry.title: Lake Worth neighbors fear deteriorating private road could cut off emergency access
entry.summary: Residents along Brooklyn Lane in Lake Worth say their only road in and out of the neighborhood is deteriorating, raising concerns about whether emergency vehicles will be able to reach their homes. 'You know it's one way in, one way out, so we're in trouble,' resident Gerald Hruby said. WATCH: Lake Worth neighbors fear deteriorating private road could cut off emergency access Residents along Brooklyn Lane say their only road in and out is deteriorating For neighbor Doug Rua, a former EMT and police officer, the biggest concern is public safety. 'I'm concerned about fire trucks being able to maneuver around it or over it, along with ambulances,' Rua said. 'So its really, its really a public safety issue.' Residents say the problem involves a pipe underneath the road. 'The road is corroding away because of a hole in the pipe under the road,' resident Richard Scott said. 'The county won't fix it, and we've had this problem since, uh, 2019.' Residents said the worsening conditions have also affected trash collection. They said garbage pickup stopped when the road became too damaged for trucks to safely navigate. WPTV has been following the neighbors concerns. During a recent return to Brooklyn Lane, WPTV traffic reporter Johann Hoffend saw county workers assessing the damage and performing temporary work that allowed trash pickup to resume. 'We reached out to WPTV earlier this month and actually last month, and theyve really been a help to us,' Rua said. But those temporary repairs are already showing signs of deterioration following recent heavy rain. The county has said it cannot repair the road because Brooklyn Lane is private. That leaves residents questioning what a permanent solution might look like and who ultimately bears responsibility for fixing the deteriorating roadway. WPTV reached out to the county about whether there are options to address the damage along Brooklyn Lane. The county said it is looking into the issue.

entry.article_text: A welfare check on an 88-year-old Okeechobee County veteran led to the discovery of a homicide and the arrest of the victim's grandson following an early-morning police chase in Indian River County, Sheriff Eric Flowers and Chief Deputy Michael Hazellief said Thursday during a press conference.WATCH BELOW: Sheriff, chief deputy announce arrest of wanted suspectPaul Eugene Baker, a longtime Okeechobee County resident and veteran, was found dead on his property after his daughter-in-law called for a welfare check. His grandson, 35-year-old Earl Douglas Wadlington III, was taken into custody after deputies pursued him through a Walmart parking lot at approximately 4 a.m."What started off as a simple welfare check of an 88-year-old veteran in our county has turned into a tragedy and a family tragedy," Hazellief said.Baker's daughter-in-law had not seen or heard from him in several days. She went to his residence and found the house in disarray, which investigators said was highly unusual."She hadn't seen him or talked to him in several days. She went by to check on the residence. She found the house in disarray, became concerned, and it was highly unusual for him to not be around or for the house to be in this manner," Hazellief said.Law enforcement obtained and executed a search warrant for the property. Baker was found dead on the property. Investigators said the manner and location of his death made it immediately evident that it was a homicide.Baker's only vehicle was also missing from the residence, along with other property. Investigators learned that Wadlington had recently been living with Baker.The daughter-in-law told investigators that Wadlington had a history with the criminal justice system and that no other family member would allow him to live with them. Wadlington has over 800 felonies in his criminal background, the chief deputy said."The daughter-in-law also explained to us that he had been in and out of prison, that he had challenges that nobody else in the family would allow him to live with him, but the grandfather had allowed him to stay there," Hazellief said.Because the daughter-in-law also held power of attorney for Baker, law enforcement was able to enter the missing vehicle into the ALPR system — a license plate reader network connected to partner agencies across the Treasure Coast area — as stolen. The vehicle was flagged as connected to a homicide suspect. Investigators tracked the vehicle leaving the area but chose not to issue a public alert."We didn't put anything out publicly at that time because we did not want to startle. We wanted the suspect to stay in the vehicle. Quite honestly, we wanted to keep driving," Hazellief said.WATCH BELOW: Dashcam video of chase, bodycam video of arrest in Indian River CountyInvestigators noted that while the agency was required this past month to remove Flock cameras from state roads and permitted locations per a state DOT order, cameras in other qualifying locations remained operational and allowed investigators to move forward with the case."To be specific with the language, we still have them in place in places that don't meet that criteria, and because of that, we were able to really move forward with this case," Hazellief said.Senior detective Ashley Rojas and her team led the investigation, the chief deputy said.The stolen vehicle was detected by Indian River County's Flock camera system this morning, leading investigators to the suspect's location.Indian River County Sheriff Flowers described the early-morning pursuit caught on video, in which Wadlington fled from deputies through a Walmart parking lot."One of the particular things that's interesting is it's 4 o'clock in the morning. He's running from our deputies. He's running through the Walmart parking lot. You see that our deputies were able to deploy stop sticks. The reason that he ultimately stopped and got out and ran is because his truck was going to stop working. That stolen vehicle is going to stop working," Flowers said.Sebastian Police Department also responded and assisted Indian River County deputies throughout the pursuit."Doesn't matter if the uniform is green or blue, doesn't matter what color it is. We're all going to go after the bad guys," Flowers said.Flowers praised the Flock camera system and said the county will continue using it despite public criticism."For all the naysayers and all the people who don't like flock and who don't like it, we're going to continue to use it. We're going to continue to put bad guys in jail because of it," Flowers said.Flowers noted that Indian River County cameras not covered by the state DOT order remain in operation. He said the Flock system has aided in other cases, including one involving a missing elderly woman.Wadlington was arrested on fleeing and eluding charges, deputies said, in addition to driving a stolen a vehicle. Both agencies said they are working very closely with the state attorney's office to obtain a warrant for his arrest for the homicide very soon."This guy is the definition of somebody who needs to stay behind bars," Flowers said.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: Treasure Coast water tank in the running for a national award - WPBF
entry.summary: Treasure Coast water tank in the running for a national award    WPBF
entry.article_text: A water tank at Jaycee Park has been transformed into a colorful tribute to Florida’s native wildlife thanks to Stuart-born and raised artist Christian Stanley and his wife, Jessica. "We keep an eye on the happenings that are going on here in Fort Pierce and saw that there was an open call to artists and put together a design that we thought was a strong submission and submitted it, and we're fortunately selected to come out here and paint the tank," said Stanley, co-owner of C. The decades-old, 22-foot-tall tank that can hold a million gallons of water is owned by Fort Pierce Utilities Authority. It was once a bright shade of white; now it features colorful paintings of manatees, dolphins, turtles, fish and pelicans, along with a sunset. "The great joy that I get out of being of mural artist is taking stuff from the ocean, from the forest, whatever, and bringing it out to the streets for people to see in a much larger-than-life fashion," he said. "So, when I knew the call was interested in being kind of native Florida wildlife, I knew that we could really bring something together that would be really impactful for the community." On Tuesday, Stanley and his wife traveled from Central Florida to the Treasure Coast to apply a UV clear coat to help protect the artwork against the harsh environment of the shore. The two originally began painting the tank in August, completing the mural within a month. He said they then decided to enter their work into Tnemec Company, Inc.'s 2026 Tank of the Year, not expecting much. But became the only South Florida water tank in the running against dozens across the state and the country. "We're so excited," Stanley said.

entry.title: South Florida fitness company brings personal trainers directly to clients
entry.summary: Having access to a gym is one thing. Actually using it is another. For Jennifer Fink, working out at home means avoiding some of the things she dislikes about going to a traditional gym. WATCH BELOW: Fitness at Your Door brings fitness trainers to your doorstep Fitness at Your Door: South Florida fitness company brings personal trainers directly to clients 'I don't really like the gym, and I usually work out at home,' Fink said. 'You don't have to wait for machines or deal with people at the gym if you don't want to.' It's one of the barriers Kashawn Fraser is trying to address through Fitness at Your Door, a South Florida wellness company that brings personal trainers directly to clients. Fraser said the company has grown to more than 250 certified personal trainers who undergo background checks, serving clients from Miami to Jupiter. The program is also expanding to the Treasure Coast. 'You can order Uber food to your door ... but to have someone show up for you where it matters the most, that's why this company was born,' Fraser said. WPTV reporter Christy Waite connected with Fraser to learn why he founded the organization. After playing professional football in the Canadian Football League and having multiple knee surgeries, he shifted his focus from his own fitness to helping others with theirs. 'I had three reconstructive knee surgeries back to back,' Fraser said. 'I have been in your shoes. I've been hurt, I've been down, I've been out of shape, I've been in shape.' For clients like Fink, having a trainer come to them can also take some of the anxiety out of going to a gym. 'You don't want to be on one of those YouTube videos where you are doing it wrong, and people are laughing at you,' Fink said. The program also works with people living in 55-and-older communities. Fraser said staying active can be especially meaningful for people approaching retirement who want the energy to enjoy time with their families. 'You work so hard to get to retirement to enjoy your kids and grandkids and have the best energy you can,' Fraser said. Across residential communities, gyms, fitness centers and clubhouses can go underused, even though residents have those amenities close to home. Fraser saw an opportunity to bring the workout into those spaces by having personal trainers meet clients where they already live.

entry.title: Okeechobee County Sheriff's Office seeks public's help on homicide suspect's movements before arrest
entry.summary: The Okeechobee County Sheriff's Office is asking for the public's assistance in gathering additional information regarding the movements of homicide suspect Earl Douglas Wadlington III prior to his arrest . WATCH: Sheriff, chief deputy announce arrest of wanted suspect Indian River, Okeechobee sheriffs announce apprehension of suspect Wadlington was arrested early Thursday morning in Indian River County following an early-morning deputy chase. Deputies said a welfare check on 88-year-old Paul Eugene Baker, an Okeechobee County veteran, led to the discovery of his death and the arrest of Wadlington, the victim's grandson. Deputies are asking anyone who may have encountered Wadlington, observed him, or has information regarding his whereabouts between Sunday, Oct. 11, and his arrest in Indian River County on Thursday, Oct. 15 at approximately 3 a.m., to please come forward. Authorities said they are particularly interested in any sightings or interactions in Palm Beach, Martin and St. Lucie counties during this timeframe. WATCH: Suspect tracked down using license plate readers, deputies say Okeechobee homicide suspect tracked down using license plate readers, deputies say Photographs show Wadlington on the day he left Okeechobee and at the time of his arrest, deputies said, and they want the community to pay special attention to the noticeable change in his hairstyle and overall appearance. Deputies said even the smallest detail could help investigators establish a more complete timeline of his movements. Anyone who saw Wadlington, spoke with him, or have any information that may assist in their investigation, please contact Senior Detective Ashley Rojas with the Okeechobee County Sheriff's Office at 863-763-3117 Ext 5108.

entry.title: Palm Beach County launches new voter app ahead of 2026 General Election
entry.summary: Palm Beach County voters now have a new way to check their voter information, find voting locations and track vote-by-mail ballots ahead of the 2026 General Election. Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections Wendy Sartory Link announced the launch of the free Vote Palm Beach mobile app ahead of Election Day on Tuesday, Nov. 3. SPECIAL SECTION: More election coverage, early voting locations The app is available through the Apple App Store and Google Play Store and is designed to give voters access to election information and services from their phones. 'Whether you're at home, at work, or on the go, we want to make it as easy as possible for every Palm Beach County voter to access accurate, reliable election information,' Link said in a Friday news release. According to the Supervisor of Elections Office, voters can use the app to: Check their voter information and registration Find voting locations View election dates and deadlines Track a vote-by-mail ballot Access information directly from the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections Office 'With the 2026 General Election approaching, our new mobile app puts another trusted resource right in the palm of your hand,' Link said. 'It's all about meeting voters where they are and giving them the tools they need to vote with confidence.' The Elections Office said the launch follows a recent overhaul of its website and the introduction of the Palm Beach County Voter Dashboard, which also provides access to voter information and election services. The Vote Palm Beach app is available for free through the Apple App Store and Google Play Store. Voters can find additional information at VotePalmBeach.gov or call the Supervisor of Elections Office at 561-656-6200.

Deputies responded to the scene along Southeast Citrus Way and spent hours investigating. Authorities said one person was detained for questioning. Harriet Ford Greg, who said the victim was her grandson, shared that he lived with her. She recalled hearing three gunshots while she was in bed and immediately worrying about him, knowing he was out that night. When she stepped outside, she said she saw him on the ground as first responders tried to save him. " laying on the ground out there and the police officer was reviving him," Greg said. entry.title: American Heritage Delray senior Domenick Swanson commits to play football at Army while chasing a state title
entry.summary: The American Heritage Stallions are chasing a back-to-back 4A state football championship, and one of the players anchoring their offensive line has already secured his spot at the next level. Domenick Swanson, a senior at American Heritage in Delray, has committed to play college football at the United States Military Academy at West Point, New York. WATCH BELOW: American Heritage Delray offensive lineman commits to play football at Army American Heritage Delray offensive lineman commits to play football at Army 'I will be going to West Point to play football,' Swanson said. 'It is a great opportunity. I went up there, and I was talking to coaches, and everyone says it's an amazing campus. It's beautiful. I mean, it's such a great opportunity to join the military and serve my country and the ability to play college football. I'm very excited about it.' Swanson wears No. 66 and plays center a role he and his coach describe as the quarterback of the offensive line. 'You know, a big reason why our coach likes me at center is that it's like the leader of the offensive line. Being there for the guys and helping with all the plays, and it's a really important part,' Swanson said. Swanson also has family support behind him, his cousin Lily, saying Swanson is a football superstar. 'Lily's my biggest cheerleader.' Swanson said. As his high school career winds down, Swanson said what he will miss most is the bonds he has built with his teammates. 'Really just the relationships and bonds that I've made with my team. You know, I just, it's going to be sad to leave them all behind. Of course, you know, I'll always have my brothers, you know, we'll always be together, but playing football with them, it'll definitely be a big change.' Swanson said. At the college level, Swanson said he looks forward to performing on a bigger stage and playing in front of thousands of people. Before he gets there, he has one goal left for this season. 'I would love to see us just go win every other game. That's kind of an obvious answer. But then, you know, we got our state championship. Hopefully we can go back-to-back,' Swanson said. The Stallions are 7-1 heading into their Friday night game vs. Lakeland Christian.
