entry.title: Port St. Lucie residents could pay about $11 more a month for trash - WPBF
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie residents could pay about $11 more a month for trash    WPBF
entry.article_text: Lucie residents are being asked in a straw poll whether they would support paying more for an additional weekly trash pickup, with the proposal adding at least $131 annually to the residential solid-waste assessment. Stay up to date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 Right now, residents receive one garbage pickup per week. The proposed change would increase costs by about $11 per month, with service potentially starting in 2028 if the city moves forward. “This is something that is nonbinding, but it gives City Council an opportunity to get a sense of the will of the people and what they would prefer to see,” said Scott Samples, spokesperson for the city of Port St. The city emphasized that the poll is not a final decision. A "yes" vote would indicate support for the additional cost, while a "no" vote would signal opposition. However, the results will not automatically change the current trash pickup schedule. City Council controls the trash contract and service levels, meaning any changes would require council approval and an updated agreement with the current waste management provider, FCC Environmental Services. The city also noted that a second pickup would be an ongoing expense and could increase with inflation. “City Council would take this up. They would have to work with the vendor to understand what the logistics of that would be. And then, the City Council would then vote on whether or not to move forward with this,” Samples said. The poll aims to provide city leaders with insight into residents' preferences, but the final decision will rest with the City Council. Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app.

entry.title: Fort Pierce police investigate after body found in Lincoln Park lake - cw34.com
entry.summary: Fort Pierce police investigate after body found in Lincoln Park lake    cw34.com
entry.article_text: A man in his 30s was found dead in a lake at Lincoln Park in Fort Pierce Wednesday morning, and police are investigating how he ended up in the water. An officer was flagged down by a citizen just after 9 a.m. who reported seeing a body floating in the lake near the 400 block of North 13th Street, Fort Pierce Police Major Michael Santiago said. Officers say they arrived and found a man face down in the water. Rescue crews pulled him out, but he was pronounced dead. Police identified the man but are waiting to notify his next of kin. Santiago described him as a Black man believed to be between 30 and 32 years old. Investigators are working to determine how the man entered the water and what he was doing before his death. See also: Man fatally shot by PBSO deputy after Boynton Beach pursuit identified There were no apparent signs of trauma to the man's body, Santiago said, but he noted the body appeared to have been in the water for some time. Police are canvassing the area, speaking with potential witnesses and looking for surveillance footage that could help investigators determine how the man ended up in the lake, per FPPD. Santiago said investigators are also looking into whether currents in the waterway could have played a role in where the body was found. It is too early to determine whether foul play or drugs were involved. Investigators are waiting for the medical examiner's findings, including autopsy and toxicology results, to help determine the cause of death. CBS12 News will provide updates as more information becomes available.

entry.title: Will Port St. Lucie see more floods this weekend? - WPEC
entry.summary: Will Port St. Lucie see more floods this weekend?    WPEC
entry.article_text: This weekend we're expected to see more heavy rain in our area. This may be exactly the kind of weekend forecast that many people in Port St. Lucie do not want to hear. Last week, parts of the city flooded when torrential rains hit Port St. According to our Stormtrac meteorologists, the city got about four inches of rain in a 48 hour period last week. Roads turned into lakes, water levels in canals rose quickly, and some drivers took their chances and drove through standing water deep enough to possibly leave them stalled with nowhere to go. One homeowner, who has a canal directly behind his house, says the flooding was unlike anything he had ever seen in the two years he's lived in Port St. See also: Trump expected at Mar-a-Lago as Palm Beach road closures, No Kings rallies are planned "When I came out, I was like, Oh, my God. I've never seen it like this before!" said Peter Rodriguez, who lives at the intersection of SW Todd Avenue and SW Broadview Street in Port St. How concerned is he about the possibility of another flood this weekend? "I don't think it's gonna get that high. If it starts getting that high, then I'm gonna start to pray. Not another flood," he said. A city spokesman says they'll have public works employees on standby this weekend if heavy rain comes, and they need to clear storm drains or move pumps into position to lower water levels in certain areas such as near the intersection of Savona Boulevard California Boulevard.

Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections Wendy Sartory Link announced the launch of the free Vote Palm Beach mobile app ahead of Election Day on Tuesday, Nov. 3. SPECIAL SECTION: More election coverage, early voting locations The app is available through the Apple App Store and Google Play Store and is designed to give voters access to election information and services from their phones. 'Whether you're at home, at work, or on the go, we want to make it as easy as possible for every Palm Beach County voter to access accurate, reliable election information,' Link said in a Friday news release. According to the Supervisor of Elections Office, voters can use the app to: Check their voter information and registration Find voting locations View election dates and deadlines Track a vote-by-mail ballot Access information directly from the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections Office 'With the 2026 General Election approaching, our new mobile app puts another trusted resource right in the palm of your hand,' Link said. 'It's all about meeting voters where they are and giving them the tools they need to vote with confidence.' The Elections Office said the launch follows a recent overhaul of its website and the introduction of the Palm Beach County Voter Dashboard, which also provides access to voter information and election services. The Vote Palm Beach app is available for free through the Apple App Store and Google Play Store. Voters can find additional information at VotePalmBeach.gov or call the Supervisor of Elections Office at 561-656-6200.

entry.title: Young Stuart divers take a leap toward college scholarships, international competition and Olympic dreams
entry.summary: In life, they say, take a leap of faith. Well, a group of kids in Stuart are doing just that on a diving board. WATCH BELOW: Stuart divers take leap toward big dreams Stuart's Atlantic Diving Team teaches the Olympic sport of diving to kids of all ages,experience levels 'There are different things for different people. Some people prefer platform diving, which is much higher but fun, which I prefer. Something Ive grown to love is all the friendships that I make throughout the years,' said Grace Erickson, a local diver, who admits diving has always been her passion. 'On my preschool poster I wrote what I wanted to be when I got older was a diver,' Erickson said. That preschooler who could only dream of being a diver is fulfilling her dream as an eighth grader. 'Its been really exciting; it's new things every twist and turn, both in your head and diving off the board,' Erickson said. Her longtime coach, Osvaldo 'Pito' Alberty, thanks her for her courage and wants to see Erickson and her teammates take the sport to new levels. 'We are like a family here. We treat each other with respect and courtesy, and we push each other to do better than everyone else,' said Pito, whose passion is sharing his experience, knowledge and love for diving with young athletes with the Atlantic Diving Team in Stuart. Atlantic takes divers of all ages, backgrounds and experience levels and teaches them the Olympic sport of diving. 'The younger we get them, the better it is because over time they can get scholarships. If they want to do international diving, they can qualify for international competitions or even the Olympics,' Pito said. For divers like Erickson, she wants to take her talents to the college level, but there's a new diver whos just learning the sport, Carissa Smith. 'I was recently a gymnast and just about two months ago I started diving,' said Smith. Smith is a natural-born acrobat. At 14, she hasn't participated in her first competition because she wants to learn the basics. But for now, she admits diving is pretty fun. 'It feels like you're flying; it's exhilarating just being able to get better at my diving,' said Smith.

entry.article_text: A shooting in the Banner Lake area of Hobe Sound on Wednesday night left one person dead, according to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office. Deputies responded to the scene along Southeast Citrus Way and spent hours investigating. Authorities said one person was detained for questioning. Harriet Ford Greg, who said the victim was her grandson, shared that he lived with her. She recalled hearing three gunshots while she was in bed and immediately worrying about him, knowing he was out that night. When she stepped outside, she said she saw him on the ground as first responders tried to save him. " laying on the ground out there and the police officer was reviving him," Greg said. "I thought that he's not going to make it. Somebody shot him." Greg said she is trying to stay strong for her family but admitted she cannot bring herself to walk into the room where her grandson stayed, saying none of this feels real. The sheriff’s office is expected to release more information Thursday afternoon. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app.

entry.title: Drinking, threats and guns: New information released in fatal shooting of 21-year-old in Hobe Sound - WPBF
entry.summary: Drinking, threats and guns: New information released in fatal shooting of 21-year-old in Hobe Sound    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 21-year-old man was fatally shot Wednesday night in the Banner Lake neighborhood of Hobe Sound, and authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident. Martin County sheriff's deputies responded to the scene along Southeast Citrus Way, where they found Jarvis Preston with three gunshot wounds to the chest. "I know you're going to ask me, was it a stand your ground? And the answer is, I don't know right now," Sheriff John Budensiek said. Budensiek explained that Preston and the shooter were friends. Witnesses reported that Preston had been drinking heavily throughout the day and began threatening the shooter and others while armed with a gun. "He's talking, I'm going to shoot you, I'm going to hurt you. The shooter walks towards him, now they're at the edge of the road, at which point the deceased starts to pull out a handgun. The shooter pulls out his AR-15, actually it's a rifle, shoots him three times in the chest, and he drops right there," Budensiek said. The sheriff said the shooter called 911 and attempted life-saving efforts before Preston was flown to St. Mary’s Hospital, where he died. Preston’s grandmother, Harriet Ford Gregg, said she heard the gunshots and later saw her grandson lying on the ground. "It was Jarvis laying on the ground out there, and the police officer was reviving him," Gregg said. She shared her grief over losing Preston, who lived with her, saying his empty bedroom is now too painful to face. I'm not going in there," Gregg said. entry.title: Investigators question if fatal shooting in Hobe Sound falls under stand-your-ground law - WPBF
entry.summary: Investigators question if fatal shooting in Hobe Sound falls under stand-your-ground law    WPBF
entry.article_text: Investigators in Martin County are working to determine whether a fatal shooting in the Banner Lake neighborhood of Hobe Sound was a crime or if the shooter acted within Florida's stand-your-ground law. The Martin County Sheriff’s Office said the shooter told them he and his friend were on Southeast Citrus Way on Wednesday night when an argument escalated. According to the shooter, his friend repeatedly threatened to shoot him and even showed him a gun. "The deceased starts to pull out a handgun. The shooter pulls out his AR-15, actually, it's a rifle, shoots him three times in the chest, and he drops right there," Sheriff John Budensiek said. Family members identified the deceased as Jarvis Preston. The sheriff’s office has not released the identity of the shooter. "I know you're going to ask me, was it a stand-your-ground? And the answer is, I don't know right now," Budensiek said. Dave Aronberg, the former Palm Beach County state attorney who is not involved in this case but has experience with stand-your-ground cases, said the shooter’s account suggests it could fall under the law. "The shooter must have reasonably believed that firing the weapon was immediately necessary to prevent imminent death or great bodily harm," Aronberg said. However, Aronberg noted that if Preston did not pull a gun, never had a gun, or if the shooter was the aggressor, the stand your ground defense would not apply. "You can't start a fight, provoke the confrontation and then shoot your way out of it," Aronberg said. The sheriff said investigators are still working to locate and interview witnesses to the shooting. He added that the final decision on whether charges will be filed will be made in collaboration with the state attorney’s office. entry.title: Amendment 3 could bring rush of Florida homebuyers, impact property values
entry.summary: Amendment 3 aims to change the property tax structure in Florida by saving money for homeowners and cutting revenue for cities and counties. It could have an impact on the Florida real estate market. A 2025 study by Realtor.com suggests home values in Florida could rise 7% to 9% if the referendum passes, and some real estate professionals say there will likely be an impact. WATCH BELOW: Amendment 3 could shake up Florida housing market Amendment 3 and Real Estate 'I don't see them going up to like the 7, 8, 9, 10 percent,' says Jeff Lichtenstein of Echo Fine Properties in Palm Beach Gardens. However, he does see a possible rush of buyers entering the market. 'You better be prepared because if it happens, it will happen fast,' Lichtenstein said. 'I think there will be a mad rush to get in here, because if not, then you're waiting five years.' That's because the referendum requires homeowners to be homesteaded in Florida by Dec 31 to receive the full tax savings right away. New home buyers entering the state would have a five-year waiting period to get the full homestead exemption. The Florida Realtors is publicly supporting Amendment 3 but isn't convinced about property values rising quickly. 'The cost of home is economically driven,' Florida Realtors CEO Margy Grant. 'It's a supply and demand conversation, and when inventory increases, prices stabilize and we've seen that in recent months.' Amendment 3 needs 60% of the vote to pass on November 3.

entry.title: 33 years after uncle's murder, family asks Gov. Ron DeSantis to sign killer's death warrant
entry.summary: Thirty-three years after his uncle was murdered, Brian Kunkel is still waiting for what he considers justice. 'There's a whole host of emotions with this,' Kunkel said. 'There's a tremendous amount of anger, and now as we speak, it kind of starts to build back up again.' WATCH BELOW: 'It's time': Family seeks execution 33 years after loved one murdered Family seeks execution 33 years after man killed in West Palm Beach His uncle, Richard Kunkel, was a 32-year-old local florist remembered by his family as outgoing, generous and full of life. 'Richard was a fun-loving guy,' Brian Kunkel said. 'He had a great spirit. Very friendly. Very outgoing the type of person that literally would give you the shirt off his back.' In 1993, Richard Kunkel went to Roosters nightclub in West Palm Beach. Court records show Ronald Knight and two other men went to the gay bar looking for a man to lure away, rob and beat. 'This was all premeditated,' Brian Kunkel said. 'He knew what he was doing.' Court records show the men befriended Kunkel and convinced him to leave with them. Knight then drove him to a secluded area, where he shot and killed him. The men robbed Kunkel, stole his car and burglarized his home. 'Richard begged for his life,' Brian Kunkel said. 'He pleaded not to be shot. He was murdered in cold blood.' Two years later, Knight was charged in another killing. In May 1995, 22-year-old Brendan Meehan was lured from Heartbreakers, then a gay nightclub on Olive Avenue in West Palm Beach, taken to a secluded area and killed. Knight was convicted of both murders and sentenced to death in 1998. 'These people had purposes in life, and it's gone,' Kunkel said. A family waiting for an execution More than three decades after Richard Kunkel's murder, Knight remains on death row. Now, Kunkel is asking Gov. Ron DeSantis to sign his death warrant. 'It's been a long and arduous process,' he said. 'My grandparents are gone. They've passed without closure, and I know, at least in my grandmother's case, she died of really a broken heart.' 'This needs to be done. It needs to be finalized,' Kunkel added. His request comes as Florida carries out executions at a pace rarely seen in the state. Florida executed a record 19 people in 2025. Seventeen people have been executed so far in 2026, with two more executions scheduled. That pace has drawn concern from death penalty opponents and defense attorneys, who warn increasingly compressed timelines could put additional strain on the appeals

entry.title: Port St. Lucie tests new water sensors as weekend rain threatens flood-prone areas
entry.summary: More rain is expected this weekend across South Florida and the Treasure Coast, and WPTV is learning that Port St. Lucie Public Works is preparing. Scott Samples, communications manager with the City of Port St. Lucie, said crews spent the week clearing debris from drains and grates. WATCH BELOW: Port St. Lucie prepares for rain, flooding concerns Port St. Lucie prepares for rain, flooding concerns Samples added that water levels in retention ponds and canals are at an adequate level and won't need to be lowered. Staff have also been testing their new pilot water sensors, which will send alerts to select staff if water levels rise. 'It's a way for us to respond faster to very specific locations,' Samples said. Jennifer Collins, owner of Pets Play Grooming off California and Savona boulevards, said her staff is preparing too. 'We're nervous about this storm coming up this week,' Collins said. 'Every time it rains, we get scared.' Collins is no stranger to flooding on California and Savona boulevards. She said flooding has occurred there for years. WPTV was there when water levels rose at the intersection last week. Collins said she already sent messages to her customers for Saturday. 'We may have to reschedule their dogs. We may have to push them off to next week,' Collins said. 'Saturdays are one of our busiest days, so it does really affect us as a small business.' For long-term solutions at the intersection, the city is working on a large-scale drainage project for the Oak Hammock neighborhood, which includes raising portions of the roadway. 'When this project is completed, those problems won't be problems anymore,' Samples said. The drainage project is still in data collection before moving on to design. 'We can't work if it's raining, and that's in Florida,' Collins said. 'That's just not OK.' The project may take years until completion, but Collins said she already thought about moving her business. 'We've also talked about possibly moving, and you know that would be hard too,' Collins said. 'I just feel like it's not, not getting better.'

entry.summary: Will Port St. Lucie see more floods this weekend?    cw34.com

entry.summary: 'He just tried to ram me': Port St. Lucie man arrested after a chase ends on South Hutchinson Island    WPBF
entry.article_text: Lucie man was arrested Thursday night after leading St. Lucie County deputies on a high-speed chase that ended on South Hutchinson Island. The pursuit began in the 9600 block of South Ocean Boulevard when a Patrol Operations deputy attempted to stop the driver of a pickup truck for a traffic violation. Andrew Bolonka, the director of communications for the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, said the driver fled instead of stopping, making a U-turn and spinning donuts in the roadway, forcing other motorists to take evasive action. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates After briefly stopping, the driver made another U-turn, cut across lanes of traffic, and accelerated toward the deputy's patrol vehicle. "The deputy tries to stop the vehicle; all of a sudden, the vehicle lunges, takes off, accelerates, does another U-turn, and then starts allegedly heading straight toward the deputy. Which you can see in the body-worn camera, where the deputy makes an evasive maneuver and says, 'Oh, he almost hit me,'" Bolonka said. Members of the department's Special Investigations Unit and deputies in the air assisted in the pursuit. The driver continued to flee even after stop sticks were deployed. Deputies eventually executed a PIT maneuver along Seaway Drive, bringing the vehicle to a stop. Despite repeated verbal commands to exit the truck, the driver refused, prompting deputies to deploy pepper balls into the vehicle. The driver then surrendered and was taken into custody without further incident. The suspect, identified as 37-year-old Joshua Gallagher of Port St. Lucie, faces several charges, including aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, possession of a controlled substance without a prescription, and resisting arrest without violence. He remains in custody at the St. "When people make decisions like this, and they commit an act that puts not only the deputies and other law enforcement officers in peril, but they are also putting the general public in peril. If we can do so safely, we're going to put it to an end," Bolonka said. Authorities expressed relief that no one was injured during the incident. entry.article_text: The person shot during a shooting in Hobe Sound died Thursday, according to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office. The victim's mother identifies the shooting victim as Jarvis Preston, 21, of Hobe Sound. She says her son was shot by his best friend. She says she does not know what led to the shooting. She says Preston was not married, and he was the father of a small child. "It's just, it's dreadful, like, I can't, I can't understand what, why it expired to the way it did, because they, best friends. What escalated this to happen when it did?" said Ebony Preston, the mother of the shooting victim. The sheriff’s office began investigating the shooting Wednesday after it happened on Southeast Citrus Way, off Florida Avenue, in the Banner Lake neighborhood. Neighbors said they heard three gunshots around 8 p.m. Sheriff's Officials say Preston was armed with a handgun with a 30-clip magazine, which was recovered at the scene of the shooting Wednesday night. And they say Preston was shot and killed by his friend, who shot him from 10 feet away with an AR15 assault rifle. Now, what I gotta do, what? I gotta, like, it's horrible," Ebony Preston said. Preston's stepfather also wants answers. That's what I don't understand how it come about, 'cause they best friends," said Rodney Clemon, the victim's stepfather. Sheriff John Budensiek, Preston and his friend had been drinking earlier in the day, and Preston tried to rob his friend near their homes. "Multiple witnesses have now told us that he made threats to all kinds of people out on the street. He was yelling loudly, was extremely intoxicated, acting belligerent," Sheriff Budensiek said. The friend, who was armed with an AR15 assault rifle, came out of his house twice with his girlfriend. The second time, the friend and Jarvis Preston--who was armed with a handgun-- got into a confrontation that ended in gunfire. "The deceased (Preston) starts to pull out a handgun. Actually, it's a rifle, shoots him three times in the chest and he (Preston) drops right there," Sheriff Budensiek explained. Mary’s Medical Center in West Palm Beach and did not survive. entry.title: Prima Vista Boulevard safety plan in St. Lucie County would add raised median after 578 crashes since 2020
entry.summary: WPTV is learning that potential road improvements are coming to a busy road in Port St. Lucie. St. Lucie County staff are sharing designs and want to hear input from neighbors about a proposed project on Prima Vista Boulevard. WATCH BELOW: Neighbors weigh in on Prima Vista Boulevard changes St. Lucie County wants input on improvements to this busy road They plan to improve a section of the roadway from Airoso Boulevard to U.S. Highway 1 by removing the center left turn lanes Dan Zrallack, county engineer, said their plan is to replace the center left-turn lanes with a raised median. 'The center turn lane is often referred to as a suicide lane,' Zrallack said. 'The more turning movements you have, the more chances you have for accidents by restricting access and putting in the median turn lanes. We can kind of control where those turning movements are and protect the drivers as well as pedestrians walking along the roadway.'  According to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, there have been 578 crashes on that section of the Prima Vista Boulevard since 2020.  Zrallack said the median will make the road safer.  'Statistically, the safety improves by up to like 40 percent or more,' Zrallack said.  But not every neighbor is sold on the improvements.  Kadaysha Wilkins lives on Prima Vista Boulevard and told WPTV the median will make traveling more complicated.  'Adding medians or anything else is going to cause more chaos than good,' Wilkins said. 'Ten to 12 years of living here, I've never seen an issue with our turning lane.'  Wilkins said it'll make it more difficult to take her niece and nephew to school by using the median instead of driving across the street.  'A five-minute ride has turned into a 15-minute travel,' Wilkins said. Wilkins said trying to come home could also be an issue. 'Turning into my driveway, which could have taken two seconds, is that now going to take 15 minutes? Wilkins said.   Zrallack said he hears the concerns and hopes they can address them on Thursday night during their public meeting. 'We're hoping to get more of that by hearing from the community again and seeing what else we can do to refine the design,' Zrallack said. A second in-person public meeting for the project was held Thursday at the MidFlorida Credit Union Event Center.

entry.title: Palm Beach seawall replacement will close popular beach for 18 months
entry.summary: Behind the peach paint and scalloped edges of a familiar Palm Beach seawall is a structure that engineers say has reached the end of its useful life after more than a century of protecting the island. Now, the town is preparing for a major replacement project that will change the look of the beachfront and close the beach for about a year and a half. WATCH BELOW: Seawall replacement will close this beach for 18 months Palm Beach seawall replacement to close beach for 18 months The pastel-colored seawall has long blended into the scenery along a beach frequented by tourists and locals. Sandra Greenberg, who was visiting with her family from Virginia and has a condo in West Palm Beach, described it simply: 'It's a great beach, love it.' A tourist visiting from Costa Rica shared the sentiment, saying, 'Yes, it's perfect.' For people who live nearby, however, the beach can be more than a destination. It is part of their regular routine. 'This is where I come to, like, relax,' said Bridget St. Laurent, a local and owner of Palm Beach Beauty Lab on Palm Beach. 'It's my life, it's my backyard, I grew up here, and the fact I can just take a five-minute drive to the ocean means so much.' St. Laurent told WPTV she tries to visit once a week, if not more. But that routine is about to be interrupted. The seawall is one line of defense from hurricanes and storm surges that, over more than a century, has protected the island from what is estimated to be $7 billion in private property, along with critical infrastructure on Palm Beach. Replacing it will require a lengthy beach closure, with the project expected to keep beachgoers away for approximately a year and a half. 'A year and a half? That's so sad,' St. Laurent said after learning from WPTV how long the closure would last. For regular visitors, the project means they will have to find another stretch of sand until the work is complete. Other beach options include Singer Island to the north, as well as Phipps Beach and Lake Worth Beach to the south. When WPTV reporter Joel Lopez asked Greenberg where she might go during the closure, she didn't have an alternative in mind. 'No, you're going to have to tell me where to go,' she said. Still, Greenberg said she understands why the work needs to be done, even if that means temporarily losing access to a beach her family enjoys. 'We're going to have to do it; let's just rip that band-aid off and get it done,' Greenberg said. The preparations are expected to become visible

Other beach options include Singer Island to the north, as well as Phipps Beach and Lake Worth Beach to the south.When WPTV reporter Joel Lopez asked Greenberg where she might go during the closure, she didn't have an alternative in mind."No, you're going to have to tell me where to go," she said.Still, Greenberg said she understands why the work needs to be done, even if that means temporarily losing access to a beach her family enjoys."We're going to have to do it; let's just rip that band-aid off and get it done," Greenberg said.The preparations are expected to become visible by the end of the year, when the pastel backdrop will be covered by fencing as work gets underway on the next chapter of the seawall."It's going to be a little bit of a nuisance for now, but more importantly we need to keep this community safe," Greenberg said.For St. Laurent, the construction may keep her away for a while, but it won't keep her away permanently.Asked whether she would return once the year-and-a-half project is finished, St. Laurent said, "Absolutely, I live here; this is my backyard."A wildlife deterrent will also be created, including a turtle berm, a small wall to protect sea turtles from clashing with the construction.Engineers say the new seawall will also include the iconic scalloped border.Before construction gets underway, the town is also giving the community an opportunity to learn more about what is planned. The town engineer told WPTV that a meeting will be held on Oct. at the Town Council Chambers, where the public can listen to a presentation and ask questions about the project.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.article_text: Lucie community members had a chance to learn more about and comment on proposed safety changes to Prima Vista Boulevard during a county information session at the MidFlorida Credit Union Event Center Thursday. The proposal focuses on the stretch between Aroso Boulevard and U.S. It would replace the center turn lane with a raised median and add landscaping designed to make the road feel narrower and encourage drivers to slow down. A majority of the community members spoke out against the plan, saying they don't believe the changes would improve safety. County officials say the changes are intended to improve safety, reduce crashes, and help slow traffic along the corridor. "We understand it's not popular. That's why we have these," said St. Lucie County engineer Dan Zrallack. "We're taking away the ease of access for people who live along this corridor. There's a lot of driveways. There's a lot of residences that have historically been able to turn directly into their driveway. It's no longer safe to do that. We have to control the traffic so that we have less accidents." County staff estimate the project could cost about $6.1 million dollars, but don't know where that money would come from yet. See also: Jupiter woman sues DoorDash, alleges delivery driver sexually assaulted her County leaders said feedback from the meeting will help shape the project. The proposal is in the early stages. Lucie County still needs to design the roadway, and identify funding sources before any work can move forward. Residents who couldn’t attend the workshop can review plans and submit comments to Christopher.arnold@stlucieco.gov.

entry.title: Policyholder advocates warn Florida homeowners of insurance challenges after Hurricane Isaias
entry.summary: As homeowners in Florida's Panhandle begin navigating insurance claims after Hurricane Isaias , policyholder advocates are sounding a warning. 'The storm after the storm is already on the way,' says Doug Quinn of the American Policyholder Association. 'An insurance system that charges more, covers less, and too often fails homeowners when they need it most.' WATCH BELOW: 'Storm after the storm': Advocates warn homeowners about insurance claims Advocates warn Florida homeowners about insurance claims after Hurricane Isaias Quinn's organization, along with Rebuild: The National Disaster Survivors Association, says insurance companies may leave many homeowners with denied claims and reduced benefits. 'America is facing a home insurance affordability crisis, and Florida families are on the front line,' said Quinn, who is currently in the Panhandle to assist homeowners. The insurance industry responded to the comments by strongly denying them. 'Bottom line is legitimate claims are not being denied,' Mark Friedlander of the Insurance Information Institute said. 'If a storm loss is covered by your wind storm coverage in your home insurance policy, those claims are covered.' Leaders in Tallahassee and insurance executives insist the insurance landscape in Florida is improving with lower rates as more insurers enter the market after litigation reforms. A poll released by the University of North Florida in September revealed that 63% of Floridians are more concerned about insurance costs than property taxes.

Harriet Ford Greg, who said the victim was her grandson, shared that he lived with her. She recalled hearing three gunshots while she was in bed and immediately worrying about him, knowing he was out that night. When she stepped outside, she said she saw him on the ground as first responders tried to save him. " laying on the ground out there and the police officer was reviving him," Greg said. entry.title: Will Port St. Lucie see more floods this weekend? - cw34.com
entry.summary: Will Port St. Lucie see more floods this weekend?    cw34.com
entry.article_text: This weekend we're expected to see more heavy rain in our area. This may be exactly the kind of weekend forecast that many people in Port St. Lucie do not want to hear. Last week, parts of the city flooded when torrential rains hit Port St. According to our Stormtrac meteorologists, the city got about four inches of rain in a 48 hour period last week. Roads turned into lakes, water levels in canals rose quickly, and some drivers took their chances and drove through standing water deep enough to possibly leave them stalled with nowhere to go. One homeowner, who has a canal directly behind his house, says he was stunned to see the extent of the flooding. It was the worst he's seen in the two years he's lived in Port St. See also: Trump expected at Mar-a-Lago as Palm Beach road closures, No Kings rallies are planned "When I came out, I was like, Oh, my God! I've never seen it like this before!" said Peter Rodriguez, who lives at the intersection of SW Todd Avenue and SW Broadview Street in Port St. How concerned is he about the possibility of another flood this weekend? "I don't think it's gonna get that high. If it starts getting that high, then I'm gonna start to pray. Not another flood," he said. Luckily floodwater did not get into his house. But the water was deep enough he says, to prevent him from driving out of his driveway. One resident says he feels the city of Port St. Lucie could be doing more to prevent such flooding. "I really think they should do something, I mean really to take care of business, you know because we pay our taxes," said Frank Camarda, a Port St. Lucie resident on SW Leisure Lane. A city spokesman says they'll have Public Works employees on standby this weekend if heavy rain comes, if they need to clear storm drains or move pumps into position to lower water levels in certain areas such as near the intersection of Savona Boulevard and SW California Boulevard. That area has been prone to flooding in the past. "They've been monitoring the canals and the retention ponds. And again, they haven't had to lower them this week which is a good sign. They're where they think they need to be. So, we're as prepared as we can be. You never know what Mother Nature is going to throw at you, but this team is doing everything it can to try to to mitigate the risks as much as possible," said Scott Samples, Strategic Communications Manager and Public Information Officer, city of Port St. He says the city of Port St. Lucie received no reports last week that floodwaters got into any homes or businesses.

entry.article_text: Lucie man was arrested Thursday night after leading St. Lucie County deputies on a high-speed chase that ended on South Hutchinson Island. The pursuit began in the 9600 block of South Ocean Boulevard when a Patrol Operations deputy attempted to stop the driver of a pickup truck for a traffic violation. Andrew Bolonka, the director of communications for the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, said the driver fled instead of stopping, making a U-turn and spinning donuts in the roadway, forcing other motorists to take evasive action. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates After briefly stopping, the driver made another U-turn, cut across lanes of traffic, and accelerated toward the deputy's patrol vehicle. "The deputy tries to stop the vehicle; all of a sudden, the vehicle lunges, takes off, accelerates, does another U-turn, and then starts allegedly heading straight toward the deputy. Which you can see in the body-worn camera, where the deputy makes an evasive maneuver and says, 'Oh, he almost hit me,'" Bolonka said. Members of the department's Special Investigations Unit and deputies in the air assisted in the pursuit. The driver continued to flee even after stop sticks were deployed. Deputies eventually executed a PIT maneuver along Seaway Drive, bringing the vehicle to a stop. Despite repeated verbal commands to exit the truck, the driver refused, prompting deputies to deploy pepper balls into the vehicle. The driver then surrendered and was taken into custody without further incident. The suspect, identified as 37-year-old Joshua Gallagher of Port St. Lucie, faces several charges, including aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, possession of a controlled substance without a prescription, and resisting arrest without violence. He remains in custody at the St. "When people make decisions like this, and they commit an act that puts not only the deputies and other law enforcement officers in peril, but they are also putting the general public in peril. If we can do so safely, we're going to put it to an end," Bolonka said. Authorities expressed relief that no one was injured during the incident. entry.title: 33 years after uncle's murder, family asks Gov. Ron DeSantis to sign killer's death warrant
entry.summary: Thirty-three years after his uncle was murdered, Brian Kunkel is still waiting for what he considers justice. 'There's a whole host of emotions with this,' Kunkel said. 'There's a tremendous amount of anger, and now as we speak, it kind of starts to build back up again.' WATCH BELOW: 'It's time': Family seeks execution 33 years after loved one murdered Family seeks execution 33 years after man killed in West Palm Beach His uncle, Richard Kunkel, was a 32-year-old local florist remembered by his family as outgoing, generous and full of life. 'Richard was a fun-loving guy,' Brian Kunkel said. 'He had a great spirit. Very friendly. Very outgoing the type of person that literally would give you the shirt off his back.' In 1993, Richard Kunkel went to Roosters nightclub in West Palm Beach. Court records show Ronald Knight and two other men went to the gay bar looking for a man to lure away, rob and beat. 'This was all premeditated,' Brian Kunkel said. 'He knew what he was doing.' Court records show the men befriended Kunkel and convinced him to leave with them. Knight then drove him to a secluded area, where he shot and killed him. The men robbed Kunkel, stole his car and burglarized his home. 'Richard begged for his life,' Brian Kunkel said. 'He pleaded not to be shot. He was murdered in cold blood.' Two years later, Knight was charged in another killing. In May 1995, 22-year-old Brendan Meehan was lured from Heartbreakers, then a gay nightclub on Olive Avenue in West Palm Beach, taken to a secluded area and killed. Knight was convicted of both murders and sentenced to death in 1998. 'These people had purposes in life, and it's gone,' Kunkel said. A family waiting for an execution More than three decades after Richard Kunkel's murder, Knight remains on death row. Now, Kunkel is asking Gov. Ron DeSantis to sign his death warrant. 'It's been a long and arduous process,' he said. 'My grandparents are gone. They've passed without closure, and I know, at least in my grandmother's case, she died of really a broken heart.' 'This needs to be done. It needs to be finalized,' Kunkel added. His request comes as Florida carries out executions at a pace rarely seen in the state. Florida executed a record 19 people in 2025. Seventeen people have been executed so far in 2026, with two more executions scheduled. That pace has drawn concern from death penalty opponents and defense attorneys, who warn increasingly compressed timelines could put additional strain on the appeals

entry.title: Will Port St. Lucie see more floods this weekend? - WPEC
entry.summary: Will Port St. Lucie see more floods this weekend?    WPEC
entry.article_text: This weekend we're expected to see more heavy rain in our area. This may be exactly the kind of weekend forecast that many people in Port St. Lucie do not want to hear. Last week, parts of the city flooded when torrential rains hit Port St. According to our Stormtrac meteorologists, the city got about four inches of rain in a 48 hour period last week. Roads turned into lakes, water levels in canals rose quickly, and some drivers took their chances and drove through standing water deep enough to possibly leave them stalled with nowhere to go. One homeowner, who has a canal directly behind his house, says he was stunned to see the extent of the flooding. It was the worst he's seen in the two years he's lived in Port St. See also: Trump expected at Mar-a-Lago as Palm Beach road closures, No Kings rallies are planned "When I came out, I was like, Oh, my God! I've never seen it like this before!" said Peter Rodriguez, who lives at the intersection of SW Todd Avenue and SW Broadview Street in Port St. How concerned is he about the possibility of another flood this weekend? "I don't think it's gonna get that high. If it starts getting that high, then I'm gonna start to pray. Not another flood," he said. Luckily floodwater did not get into his house. But the water was deep enough he says, to prevent him from driving out of his driveway. One resident says he feels the city of Port St. Lucie could be doing more to prevent such flooding. "I really think they should do something, I mean really to take care of business, you know because we pay our taxes," said Frank Camarda, a Port St. Lucie resident on SW Leisure Lane. A city spokesman says they'll have Public Works employees on standby this weekend if heavy rain comes, if they need to clear storm drains or move pumps into position to lower water levels in certain areas such as near the intersection of Savona Boulevard and SW California Boulevard. That area has been prone to flooding in the past. "They've been monitoring the canals and the retention ponds. And again, they haven't had to lower them this week which is a good sign. They're where they think they need to be. So, we're as prepared as we can be. You never know what Mother Nature is going to throw at you, but this team is doing everything it can to try to to mitigate the risks as much as possible," said Scott Samples, Strategic Communications Manager and Public Information Officer, city of Port St. He says the city of Port St. Lucie received no reports last week that floodwaters got into any homes or businesses.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie tests new water sensors as weekend rain threatens flood-prone areas - WFLX
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie tests new water sensors as weekend rain threatens flood-prone areas    WFLX
entry.article_text: More rain is expected this weekend across South Florida and the Treasure Coast, and WPTV is learning that Port St. Lucie Public Works is preparing. Scott Samples, communications manager with the City of Port St. Lucie, said crews spent the week clearing debris from drains and grates. Lucie prepares for rain, flooding concerns Samples added that water levels in retention ponds and canals are at an adequate level and won't need to be lowered. Staff have also been testing their new pilot water sensors, which will send alerts to select staff if water levels rise. "It's a way for us to respond faster to very specific locations," Samples said. Jennifer Collins, owner of Pets Play Grooming off California and Savona boulevards, said her staff is preparing too. "We're nervous about this storm coming up this week," Collins said. "Every time it rains, we get scared." Collins is no stranger to flooding on California and Savona boulevards. She said flooding has occurred there for years. WPTV was there when water levels rose at the intersection last week. Collins said she already sent messages to her customers for Saturday. "We may have to reschedule their dogs. We may have to push them off to next week," Collins said. "Saturdays are one of our busiest days, so it does really affect us as a small business." For long-term solutions at the intersection, the city is working on a large-scale drainage project for the Oak Hammock neighborhood, which includes raising portions of the roadway. "When this project is completed, those problems won't be problems anymore," Samples said. The drainage project is still in data collection before moving on to design. "We can't work if it's raining, and that's in Florida," Collins said. "That's just not OK." The project may take years until completion, but Collins said she already thought about moving her business. "We've also talked about possibly moving, and you know that would be hard too," Collins said. "I just feel like it's not, not getting better."

According to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, there have been 578 crashes on that section of the Prima Vista Boulevard since 2020. Zrallack said the median will make the road safer.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie tests new water sensors as weekend rain threatens flood-prone areas - WFLX
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie tests new water sensors as weekend rain threatens flood-prone areas    WFLX
entry.article_text: More rain is expected this weekend across South Florida and the Treasure Coast, and WPTV is learning that Port St. Lucie Public Works is preparing. Scott Samples, communications manager with the City of Port St. Lucie, said crews spent the week clearing debris from drains and grates. Lucie prepares for rain, flooding concerns Samples added that water levels in retention ponds and canals are at an adequate level and won't need to be lowered. Staff have also been testing their new pilot water sensors, which will send alerts to select staff if water levels rise. "It's a way for us to respond faster to very specific locations," Samples said. Jennifer Collins, owner of Pets Play Grooming off California and Savona boulevards, said her staff is preparing too. "We're nervous about this storm coming up this week," Collins said. "Every time it rains, we get scared." Collins is no stranger to flooding on California and Savona boulevards. She said flooding has occurred there for years. WPTV was there when water levels rose at the intersection last week. Collins said she already sent messages to her customers for Saturday. "We may have to reschedule their dogs. We may have to push them off to next week," Collins said. "Saturdays are one of our busiest days, so it does really affect us as a small business." For long-term solutions at the intersection, the city is working on a large-scale drainage project for the Oak Hammock neighborhood, which includes raising portions of the roadway. "When this project is completed, those problems won't be problems anymore," Samples said. The drainage project is still in data collection before moving on to design. "We can't work if it's raining, and that's in Florida," Collins said. "That's just not OK." The project may take years until completion, but Collins said she already thought about moving her business. "We've also talked about possibly moving, and you know that would be hard too," Collins said. "I just feel like it's not, not getting better."

entry.title: South Florida fitness company brings personal trainers directly to clients
entry.summary: Having access to a gym is one thing. Actually using it is another. For Jennifer Frink, working out at home means avoiding some of the things she dislikes about going to a traditional gym. WATCH BELOW: Fitness at Your Door brings fitness trainers to your doorstep Fitness at Your Door: South Florida fitness company brings personal trainers directly to clients 'I don't really like the gym, and I usually work out at home,' Frink said. 'You don't have to wait for machines or deal with people at the gym if you don't want to.' It's one of the barriers Kashawn Fraser is trying to address through Fitness at Your Door, a South Florida wellness company that brings personal trainers directly to clients. Fraser said the company has grown to more than 250 certified personal trainers who undergo background checks, serving clients from Miami to Jupiter. The program is also expanding to the Treasure Coast. 'You can order Uber food to your door ... but to have someone show up for you where it matters the most, that's why this company was born,' Fraser said. WPTV reporter Christy Waite connected with Fraser to learn why he founded the organization. After playing professional football in the Canadian Football League and having multiple knee surgeries, he shifted his focus from his own fitness to helping others with theirs. 'I had three reconstructive knee surgeries back to back,' Fraser said. 'I have been in your shoes. I've been hurt, I've been down, I've been out of shape, I've been in shape.' For clients like Frink, having a trainer come to them can also take some of the anxiety out of going to a gym. 'You don't want to be on one of those YouTube videos where you are doing it wrong, and people are laughing at you,' Frink said. The program also works with people living in 55-and-older communities. Fraser said staying active can be especially meaningful for people approaching retirement who want the energy to enjoy time with their families. 'You work so hard to get to retirement to enjoy your kids and grandkids and have the best energy you can,' Fraser said. Across residential communities, gyms, fitness centers and clubhouses can go underused, even though residents have those amenities close to home. Fraser saw an opportunity to bring the workout into those spaces by having personal trainers meet clients where they already live.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie residents weigh in on proposed Prima Vista Boulevard safety changes - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie residents weigh in on proposed Prima Vista Boulevard safety changes    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie community members had a chance to learn more about and comment on proposed safety changes to Prima Vista Boulevard during a county information session at the MidFlorida Credit Union Event Center Thursday. The proposal focuses on the stretch between Aroso Boulevard and U.S. It would replace the center turn lane with a raised median and add landscaping designed to make the road feel narrower and encourage drivers to slow down. A majority of the community members spoke out against the plan, saying they don't believe the changes would improve safety. County officials say the changes are intended to improve safety, reduce crashes, and help slow traffic along the corridor. "We understand it's not popular. That's why we have these," said St. Lucie County engineer Dan Zrallack. "We're taking away the ease of access for people who live along this corridor. There's a lot of driveways. There's a lot of residences that have historically been able to turn directly into their driveway. It's no longer safe to do that. We have to control the traffic so that we have less accidents." County staff estimate the project could cost about $6.1 million dollars, but don't know where that money would come from yet. See also: Jupiter woman sues DoorDash, alleges delivery driver sexually assaulted her County leaders said feedback from the meeting will help shape the project. The proposal is in the early stages. Lucie County still needs to design the roadway, and identify funding sources before any work can move forward. Residents who couldn’t attend the workshop can review plans and submit comments to Christopher.arnold@stlucieco.gov.

entry.title: Amendment 3 could bring rush of Florida homebuyers, impact property values
entry.summary: Amendment 3 aims to change the property tax structure in Florida by saving money for homeowners and cutting revenue for cities and counties. It could also have an impact on the Florida real estate market. A 2025 study by Realtor.com suggests home values in Florida could rise 7% to 9% if the referendum passes, and some real estate professionals say there will likely be an impact. WATCH BELOW: Amendment 3 could shake up Florida housing market Amendment 3 and Real Estate 'I don't see them going up to like the 7, 8, 9, 10 percent,' says Jeff Lichtenstein of Echo Fine Properties in Palm Beach Gardens. However, he does see a possible rush of buyers entering the market. 'You better be prepared because if it happens, it will happen fast,' Lichtenstein said. 'I think there will be a mad rush to get in here, because if not, then you're waiting five years.' That's because the referendum requires homeowners to be homesteaded in Florida by Dec 31 to receive the full tax savings right away. New home buyers entering the state would have a five-year waiting period to get the full homestead exemption. The Florida Realtors is publicly supporting Amendment 3 but isn't convinced about property values rising quickly. 'The cost of home is economically driven,' Florida Realtors CEO Margy Grant. 'It's a supply and demand conversation, and when inventory increases, prices stabilize and we've seen that in recent months.' Amendment 3 needs 60% of the vote to pass on November 3.

entry.title: AmeriCorps returns to Martin County with renewed focus on boosting students' reading skills - WFLX
entry.summary: AmeriCorps returns to Martin County with renewed focus on boosting students' reading skills    WFLX
entry.article_text: A program that has worked with thousands of Martin County children is returning after a brief hiatus, with a renewed focus on helping young students strengthen their reading skills. The Boys Girls Clubs of Martin County is celebrating the return of its AmeriCorps program, which places volunteers directly with students to provide individualized and small-group academic support. WATCH BELOW: Literacy program returns to Martin County after hiatus “We missed it. It was an extremely important piece to our success and moving the district forward,” Martin County Schools Superintendent Michael Maine said. The Boys Girls Clubs of Martin County first introduced the federal mentorship program to the area in 2019. For six years, AmeriCorps volunteers worked with thousands of local students before federal funding shortfalls forced the program to pause. Now, program leaders have set new goals for its return. WPTV reporter Christy Waite connected with AmeriCorps Program Director for Martin County Boys and Girls Club, Russell Lamberti. “We want to serve 575 students, and we want to see an increase of 65% growth, and that can be in vocabulary, fluency and grammar,” AmeriCorps Program Director Russell Lamberti said. AmeriCorps volunteers will work one-on-one and in small groups with kindergarten through fifth-grade students at four Boys Girls Club locations, with an emphasis on literacy. For AmeriCorps Volunteer Experience Specialist Abelard Cesar, the mission also has a personal connection. I learned English at 13 years old, and I had mentors that helped me grow,” Cesar said. The Boys Girls Clubs says the program delivered significant academic results during its previous six-year run. In some cases, as many as eight in 10 participating students moved their reading from Level 1 to Level 4. About the same percentage maintained or improved their English Language Arts grades, according to the organization. The organization said students also showed improvements in literacy rates, assessment scores, school attendance and behavioral patterns. AmeriCorps members’ work previously extended beyond the classroom. According to the Boys Girls Clubs, volunteers completed nearly 50 service projects in Martin County and contributed more than 60,000 hours to community cleanup efforts and other acts of service. The return comes as literacy remains a focus across the county. Earlier this year, the Martin County School District reported that local kindergarten students tied for fourth place statewide in readiness scores and literacy assessments. The AmeriCorps program is part of a broader academic effort by the Boys Girls Clubs of Martin County, which serves more than 1,000 members ages 6 to 18 in its daily programs. The organization also provides after-school academic assistance through certified teachers. Beyond its Clubs, the organization runs or manages several programs serving local children, including Reading Buddies, Character Counts!, career training using virtual reality technology, culinary programs and skilled-trades programs. With AmeriCorps volunteers returning, the Boys Girls Clubs says it hopes to build on the program’s previous results while giving more Martin County students the individual attention and support they need.

entry.title: Do you know the difference between a macaroon and a macaron?
entry.summary: Do you know the difference between a macaroon and a macaron? WPTVs Christy Waite visited the GreenMarket in downtown West Palm Beach, where she learned the difference between the two and caught up with a popular local vendor making its return after a yearlong hiatus. WATCH: Do you know the difference between a macaroon and a macaron? Small business Saturday The West Palm Beach GreenMarket is more than a weekend destination. For local entrepreneurs like Jonathan Aviv, it has also provided a place to grow a small business. Aviv is the owner and master baker behind Macaroner, a small French macaron bakery offering both traditional, vegan, and gluten-free macarons in 24 flavors. Aviv said he decided to turn his love for macarons into a business during the COVID-19 pandemic. Getting the recipe right, however, took plenty of trial and error. It took a long time, thousands of macarons thrown away and wasted in the process, but eventually I cracked the code, Aviv said. For six years, Macaroner has called South Florida and Palm Beach County home. At Avivs booth, customers can find an assortment of colorful flavors, including lemon basil and salted caramel. But Aviv said theres one flavor he is especially proud of and that's his lavender honey. The lavender is a classic French flavor and he uses Mnuka honey from New Zealand. After nearly four years at the GreenMarket, Macaroner took a yearlong hiatus to focus on wholesale business. This season, the bakery is back. Aviv said he typically prepares between 1,000 and 2,000 macarons for a day at the GreenMarket so he doesn't run out of flavors. Some flavors are especially popular with younger customers. The kids go for the fun and cute flavors like birthday cake, Fruity Tooty, strawberry hibiscus and Oreo cookie, Aviv said. entry.title: Man found dead after barricade situation in St. Lucie County, deputies say
entry.summary: A man was found dead from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound Saturday after a barricade situation prompted deputies to evacuate a woman and children from a St. Lucie County home, according to the sheriffs office. The St. Lucie County Sheriffs Office said deputies responded around 10:17 a.m. to a reported domestic violence incident in the 7600 block of Winter Garden Boulevard. Deputies initially encountered a man in the front yard who went back inside after seeing law enforcement. Authorities later made contact with a man and woman at the front door. During that interaction, a deputy saw what appeared to be a firearm in the mans possession and ordered him to drop it, the sheriffs office said. Instead, the man closed the door and retreated inside, creating a barricaded-subject situation while other people remained in the home. According to investigators, the man came outside several times and said he would surrender after making a phone call, but repeatedly went back inside. During his final retreat into the home, deputies heard what appeared to be a gunshot. Knowing an adult woman and children were still inside and could be in danger, deputies entered the residence and evacuated them through a side window, the sheriffs office said. Deputies later found the man dead from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound. Authorities said there is no ongoing threat to the community. Detectives, crime scene technicians and investigators from the Medical Examiners Office are expected to remain at the scene for several hours as the investigation continues.

entry.title: Young Stuart divers take a leap toward college scholarships, international competition and Olympic dreams
entry.summary: In life, they say, take a leap of faith. Well, a group of kids in Stuart are doing just that on a diving board. WATCH BELOW: Stuart divers take leap toward big dreams Stuart's Atlantic Diving Team teaches the Olympic sport of diving to kids of all ages,experience levels 'There are different things for different people. Some people prefer platform diving, which is much higher but fun, which I prefer. Something Ive grown to love is all the friendships that I make throughout the years,' said Grace Erickson, a local diver, who admits diving has always been her passion. 'On my preschool poster I wrote what I wanted to be when I got older was a diver,' Erickson said. That preschooler who could only dream of being a diver is fulfilling her dream as an eighth grader. 'Its been really exciting; it's new things every twist and turn, both in your head and diving off the board,' Erickson said. Her longtime coach, Osvaldo 'Pito' Alberty, thanks her for her courage and wants to see Erickson and her teammates take the sport to new levels. 'We are like a family here. We treat each other with respect and courtesy, and we push each other to do better than everyone else,' said Pito, whose passion is sharing his experience, knowledge and love for diving with young athletes with the Atlantic Diving Team in Stuart. Atlantic takes divers of all ages, backgrounds and experience levels and teaches them the Olympic sport of diving. 'The younger we get them, the better it is because over time they can get scholarships. If they want to do international diving, they can qualify for international competitions or even the Olympics,' Pito said. For divers like Erickson, she wants to take her talents to the college level, but there's a new diver whos just learning the sport, Carissa Smith. 'I was recently a gymnast and just about two months ago I started diving,' said Smith. Smith is a natural-born acrobat. At 14, she hasn't participated in her first competition because she wants to learn the basics. But for now, she admits diving is pretty fun. 'It feels like you're flying; it's exhilarating just being able to get better at my diving,' said Smith.

entry.article_text: Deputies have secured an area of St. Lucie County while responding to a reported domestic battery Saturday. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office said deputies responded to the 7600 block of Winter Garden Boulevard. When deputies arrived, they saw a man in the front yard of a home. According to the sheriff’s office, the man then went back inside the residence. Deputies established a perimeter around the home and were awaiting additional SWAT resources. The sheriff’s office said the area is secured but asked residents in the immediate area to avoid the vicinity while deputies handle the situation. The response remains active. Residents should expect delays and avoid the area.

entry.title: St. Lucie County voters to decide on sales tax renewal, mosquito control expansion - WPBF
entry.summary: St. Lucie County voters to decide on sales tax renewal, mosquito control expansion    WPBF
entry.article_text: Lucie County voters will decide in November on two ballot questions aimed at addressing the county's growing population and its impact on infrastructure and services. The first question asks voters to renew the half-cent sales tax, originally approved in 2018, which is set to expire in two years. County leaders are seeking to extend the tax for another decade. This is not a new tax but would keep the total sales tax rate at 7%, with the half-cent portion funding infrastructure projects such as road improvements, sidewalks, stormwater drainage, and major projects like widening St. "Now we're seeing that impact, you know, the delayed maintenance and the increased growth we've seen picked up, we're starting to have to play catch-up with those infrastructure projects and the needs are still there," said Erick Gill, communications director for St. The second question focuses on expanding the mosquito control district to include the Tradition and southwestern areas of the county, which have grown beyond the current service boundaries. Currently, mosquito control services cover about half of the county's 600 square miles. If voters approve the expansion, affected property owners would pay about $28 more annually in taxes to fund fogging, spraying, and mosquito surveillance. Both measures will appear on the November ballot, addressing different needs as St. Lucie County continues to grow. Voters are encouraged to review their sample ballots to determine which questions apply to them before voting on Nov. entry.title: President Trump returns to Palm Beach as midterm elections approach
entry.summary: President Donald Trump returned to Palm Beach on Friday for his first trip of the season to Mar-a-Lago, bringing the heightened security and traffic impacts that accompany presidential visits as the country moves closer to the 2026 midterm elections. Trump arrived in South Florida after campaigning Friday in Dalton, Georgia, where he rallied alongside Republican candidates as the party works to turn out voters ahead of Election Day. WPTV saw supporters lining the route toward Trump's Mar-a-Lago estate as his motorcade traveled through Palm Beach. Among them was the Campbell family, who had traveled from South Carolina for a baseball tournament. 'I wasn't expecting this on my bingo card. I thought we were playing baseball,' one member of the Campbell family told WPTV. 'But I'm glad we get to see this.' Trump pushes Republican voters to turn out Trump's arrival came directly after his campaign stop at Dalton Municipal Airport in Georgia, where he appeared with Republican U.S. Senate candidate Mike Collins and gubernatorial candidate Rick Jackson. The Georgia Senate race has become a significant midterm battleground. Recent polling has shown Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff leading Collins. Trump stressed the importance of turnout during his remarks. 'When I'm not on the ballot, I guess it's a compliment, but people don't show up so much,' Trump said. 'So this is, really, I think the most important midterm election I think we've ever had.' The president also told supporters in Dalton that they should 'pretend I'm on the ballot' as he sought to boost Republican enthusiasm. Security increases around Palm Beach Back in Palm Beach, security was heightened around the island ahead of Trump's arrival. Palm Beach County Sheriff Ric Bradshaw recently told WPTV's Michael Hoffman that the county received an exemption allowing license plate reader cameras to remain on state roads as an additional layer of presidential protection. 'We filed a brief with the Department of Highway Safety up there in Tallahassee that, along with the Secret Service, and says, 'Hey, this is why we can't take them down,' and they granted us that exemption,' Bradshaw said. More presidential travel could mean traffic impacts Trump was expected to travel to Kentucky on Saturday before returning to Palm Beach later in the day, according to information provided to WPTV. Those movements are expected to bring additional closures and traffic impacts as the presidential motorcade travels through the area. Tru

entry.title: Lanes reopen after semi-truck jackknifes on Florida's Turnpike in Martin County
entry.summary: All northbound lanes of Florida's Turnpike in Martin County are back open Friday afternoon after a jackknifed semi caused heavy delays. The crash happened shortly before noon near mile marker 125, underneath the SE Bridge Road overpass. Watch traffic camera video: Semi crash on Florida Turnpike According to the Florida Highway Patrol, the truck driver lost control, causing the crash. Paramedics took one patient with minor injuries to the hospital by ground, according to Martin County Fire Rescue spokeswoman Jillian Kay. Lanes started reopening to traffic just after 1 p.m. on Friday. Kay said that the Martin County Sheriff's Office and Florida Highway Patrol also responded to the wreck and will investigate.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie tests new water sensors as weekend rain threatens flood-prone areas
entry.summary: More rain is expected this weekend across South Florida and the Treasure Coast, and WPTV is learning that Port St. Lucie Public Works is preparing. Scott Samples, communications manager with the City of Port St. Lucie, said crews spent the week clearing debris from drains and grates. WATCH BELOW: Port St. Lucie prepares for rain, flooding concerns Port St. Lucie prepares for rain, flooding concerns Samples added that water levels in retention ponds and canals are at an adequate level and won't need to be lowered. Staff have also been testing their new pilot water sensors, which will send alerts to select staff if water levels rise. 'It's a way for us to respond faster to very specific locations,' Samples said. Jennifer Collins, owner of Pets Play Grooming off California and Savona boulevards, said her staff is preparing too. 'We're nervous about this storm coming up this week,' Collins said. 'Every time it rains, we get scared.' Collins is no stranger to flooding on California and Savona boulevards. She said flooding has occurred there for years. WPTV was there when water levels rose at the intersection last week. Collins said she already sent messages to her customers for Saturday. 'We may have to reschedule their dogs. We may have to push them off to next week,' Collins said. 'Saturdays are one of our busiest days, so it does really affect us as a small business.' For long-term solutions at the intersection, the city is working on a large-scale drainage project for the Oak Hammock neighborhood, which includes raising portions of the roadway. 'When this project is completed, those problems won't be problems anymore,' Samples said. The drainage project is still in data collection before moving on to design. 'We can't work if it's raining, and that's in Florida,' Collins said. 'That's just not OK.' The project may take years until completion, but Collins said she already thought about moving her business. 'We've also talked about possibly moving, and you know that would be hard too,' Collins said. 'I just feel like it's not, not getting better.'

entry.title: President Trump returns to Palm Beach as midterm elections approach
entry.summary: President Donald Trump returned to Palm Beach on Friday for his first trip of the season to Mar-a-Lago, bringing the heightened security and traffic impacts that accompany presidential visits as the country moves closer to the 2026 midterm elections. WATCH BELOW: President Trump returns to Mar-a-Lago as election nears President Trump returns to Palm Beach as midterm elections approach Trump arrived in South Florida after campaigning Friday in Dalton, Georgia, where he rallied alongside Republican candidates as the party works to turn out voters ahead of Election Day. WPTV saw supporters lining the route toward Trump's Mar-a-Lago estate as his motorcade traveled through Palm Beach. Among them was the Campbell family, who had traveled from South Carolina for a baseball tournament. 'I wasn't expecting this on my bingo card. I thought we were playing baseball,' one member of the Campbell family told WPTV. 'But I'm glad we get to see this.' Trump pushes Republican voters to turn out Trump's arrival came directly after his campaign stop at Dalton Municipal Airport in Georgia, where he appeared with Republican U.S. Senate candidate Mike Collins and gubernatorial candidate Rick Jackson. The Georgia Senate race has become a significant midterm battleground. Recent polling has shown Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff leading Collins. Trump stressed the importance of turnout during his remarks. 'When I'm not on the ballot, I guess it's a compliment, but people don't show up so much,' Trump said. 'So this is, really, I think the most important midterm election I think we've ever had.' The president also told supporters in Dalton that they should 'pretend I'm on the ballot' as he sought to boost Republican enthusiasm. Security increases around Palm Beach Back in Palm Beach, security was heightened around the island ahead of Trump's arrival. Palm Beach County Sheriff Ric Bradshaw recently told WPTV's Michael Hoffman that the county received an exemption allowing license plate reader cameras to remain on state roads as an additional layer of presidential protection. 'We filed a brief with the Department of Highway Safety up there in Tallahassee that, along with the Secret Service, and says, 'Hey, this is why we can't take them down,' and they granted us that exemption,' Bradshaw said. More presidential travel could mean traffic impacts Trump was expected to travel to Kentucky on Saturday before returning to Palm Beach later in the day, according to information provided to WPTV.

entry.title: Man dies by suicide after barricaded-subject SWAT situation in Fort Pierce - WPEC
entry.summary: Man dies by suicide after barricaded-subject SWAT situation in Fort Pierce    WPEC
entry.article_text: A man was found dead from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound after deputies responded to a reported domestic violence incident Saturday morning in Fort Pierce's Lakewood Park neighborhood. Deputies responded around 10:17 a.m. to a home in the 7600 block of Winter Garden Boulevard, where they encountered a man in the front yard. The man went back inside after seeing law enforcement, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office . Deputies say they later contacted a man and woman at the front door. A deputy saw what appeared to be a firearm in the man's possession and ordered him to drop the weapon, but he shut the door and retreated inside, prompting a barricaded-subject situation with other occupants still in the home. See also: Driver tried to ram deputy before PIT maneuver ended chase, SLCSO says During the incident, the man reportedly came outside several times and indicated he would surrender after making a phone call, but repeatedly went back inside, deputies said. During his final retreat into the home, deputies say they heard what appeared to be a gunshot. Concerned for an adult woman and children who remained inside, deputies entered the home without alerting the occupants and evacuated them through a side window, according to the sheriff's office. Deputies later found the man dead from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound. The sheriff's office said there is no ongoing threat to the community. Detectives with the agency's Criminal Investigations Division, crime scene technicians and investigators from the Medical Examiner's Office remained at the scene to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident. If you or someone you know is struggling with thoughts of suicide, help is available. Call or text 988 to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline , available 24/7. You can also chat at 988lifeline.org
