entry.title: Rescued Hobe Sound kittens recover with foster family after being buried alive
entry.summary: Two kittens rescued after being buried alive in Hobe Sound are recovering in foster care and showing signs of remarkable progress just days after investigators say they survived a tragic act of animal cruelty. Kali and Amara, two approximately 4-week-old kittens, are now living with a Treasure Coast family after Martin County Sheriff's Office deputies rescued them from the ground last week. Authorities say 36-year-old Alba Chavez buried multiple kittens alive because she believed they were demons. The case has drawn widespread attention across the Treasure Coast, where animal advocates and residents have followed the kittens' recovery. As the community processes the disturbing allegations, Kali and Amara's survival has become a symbol of resilience and hope. Rescued Hobe Sound kittens recover with foster family after being buried alive Deputies rescued two kittens buried alive Body camera video released by the Martin County Sheriff's Office shows deputies digging to reach the kittens after receiving reports about the incident. Video captured one deputy expressing surprise that the animals were still alive as rescue efforts unfolded. WATCH: Hobe Sound woman allegedly buried kittens alive Hobe Sound woman buries kittens alive, believes they were demons According to investigators, two kittens were rescued alive. Two others were found dead, and another kitten remains missing. The incident led to criminal charges against Chavez, who the sheriff's office says is currently being held on an Immigration and Customs Enforcement hold. Foster family stepped in immediately When the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast needed help caring for the surviving kittens, local nurse Jennifer Jagdeo and her family volunteered to take them in. 'As an animal lover, I think we're all shocked by it,' Jagdeo said. Her family has experience fostering animals, and she said the decision to help was immediate. 'For me, my focus has been them and healing them,' Jagdeo said. Kali and Amara making steady progress Just days after their rescue, the kittens are becoming increasingly active. entry.article_text: Impact weather is creating hazardous conditions across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beaches on Sunday. A wind advisory is in effect for parts of Indian River County, with sustained winds of 20 to 25 miles per hour and gusts up to 40 miles per hour. Wind gusts around 30 miles per hour have already been recorded this Sunday morning from Sebastian and Vero Beach south through Jupiter, West Palm Beach, Boynton Beach and Boca Raton. Meanwhile, a high surf advisory remains in effect along the Atlantic coast, where seas are expected to reach seven to 12 feet. The rough surf is creating dangerous swimming conditions, a high risk of rip currents and the potential for beach erosion. Forecasters are also monitoring an area in the Atlantic with a 30% chance of tropical development over the next seven days, though no immediate impacts to Florida are expected. Residents are urged to secure loose outdoor items, use caution on the roads and stay out of rough ocean waters.

entry.title: Suspicious phone call prompts delays at Donald J. Trump International Airport
entry.summary: A police presence caused traffic delays around Donald J. Trump International Airport on Sunday afternoon as law enforcement investigated a suspicious phone call. In a Facebook post at 1:20 p.m., the airport said the Palm Beach County Sheriffs Office had slowed traffic entering the terminal as a precaution. Law enforcement is investigating a suspicious phone call, the airport said. As a precaution, PBSO has slowed traffic entering the terminal, and travelers may experience delays. A witness told WPTV that the airports arrivals and departures area was blocked off to vehicle traffic. The witness also said some passengers began getting out of their vehicles along Belvedere Boulevard and walking toward the airport because they were concerned they could miss their flights. The airport urged people to report any suspicious activity directly to law enforcement and thanked travelers for their patience and cooperation. WPTV has reached out to the Palm Beach County Sheriffs Office for additional details. This is a developing story. Check back for updates.

entry.title: Jupiter apartment residents raise drainage concerns after heavy rain floods parking areas
entry.summary: Residents at Marino Apartments in Jupiter are raising concerns about drainage after they say heavy rain repeatedly leaves portions of the property covered in standing water, at times forcing families to walk through the water simply to reach their vehicles. Resident James Ortman told WPTV the problem has become part of his family's routine when rain hits. He said the water has risen as high as 10 to 12 inches around the front tires of his truck at its worst. WATCH: Jupiter residents seek answers over apartment flooding Jupiter Residents Seek Answers Over Apartment Flooding | WPTV 'My 9-year-old and 5-year-old should not have to describe to me whether it's a puddle, pond, or lake outside the truck,' Ortman said. WPTV's Samantha Gutierrez has repeatedly reached out to management at Marino Apartments seeking an explanation for the drainage problems and information about what, if anything, will be done to address them. Management had not provided a comment at the time of this report. Family changes routine when water collects For Ortman, the drainage concerns are more than an inconvenience. He said the standing water can affect something as routine as getting his children into the family vehicle. 'If they do, then we may have to go more Crocs, getting them into the truck, and I'll bring their school shoes, their school socks or shoes down,' Ortman said. 'Same thing for me.' Ortman said he does not want his children walking through significant amounts of standing water to reach the vehicle. 'Would you feel comfortable walking your kids through, I don't know, 1,500 square feet of eight inches of water?' he asked. Resident wants lasting solution Ortman said he wants apartment management to understand what residents are experiencing firsthand and address why water continues to collect when heavy rain falls. 'Live through it. Live through it for a few days, and then tell me,' Ortman said. WPTV has not independently verified Ortman's estimates of the water's depth or the size of the affected area. The descriptions of those conditions are based on his account. WPTV also has not received information from Marino Apartments management explaining the cause of the reported drainage problems or whether repairs or other corrective measures are planned. For residents like Ortman, the concern now is what will happen the next time heavy rain arrives and whether conditions will change before then. The descriptions of those conditions are based on his account.WPTV also has not received information from Marino Apartments management explaining the cause of the reported drainage problems or whether repairs or other corrective measures are planned.For residents like Ortman, the concern now is what will happen the next time heavy rain arrives and whether conditions will change before then.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.summary: Protesters gather across Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast ahead of midterms    WPBF
entry.article_text: Hundreds of residents across the Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast gathered this weekend for "No Kings" protests, urging civic engagement and opposing President Donald Trump’s policies ahead of the midterm elections. Anita Smith, a protester, said, "I am really fed up with the way the institution our government is running." Roger Lyle, another protester, said, "I'm out here to protest the president of the United States because the man is a criminal and he needs to be accounted for." Despite the rain, the protests drew large crowds, with organizers emphasizing the importance of ensuring voters have a plan for the midterms. Just do a little research on what these people have done that want to get into the office, and what do you think they're going to do for you?" Lyle said. Smith added, "Nationwide, it's important because our democracy is turning into fascism and authoritarianism, and we have to correct that." The "No Kings" movement opposes the policies and actions of Trump. On Saturday, protests were planned from the Treasure Coast to southern Palm Beach County. Smith drove from Okeechobee to Port St. Lucie to protest against the current administration and Amendment 3 on property taxes. "Somebody in the fine print is going to get rich off this proposition and nobody is reading the whole thing because it's in legalese and I'm afraid people are going to just vote for it and they don't really know what they're voting for. They think they're going to get money back," Smith said. There were no counterprotesters at the rally. Early voting in the area begins Monday.

entry.title: How to find your polling place in Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast
entry.summary: Before heading to the polls for Florida's 2026 general election, voters should confirm where they are assigned to vote. Polling places can change between election cycles, and election officials recommend checking your polling location well before Election Day. Voters in Palm Beach County, St. Lucie County, Martin County, Indian River County and Okeechobee County can visit their local supervisor of elections website to verify registration information, view their sample ballot and locate their assigned polling place. How do I find my polling place? Most county election offices offer online voter lookup tools that allow voters to: Verify voter registration status View a sample ballot Find their precinct Locate their Election Day polling site Confirm district assignments Can I vote at any polling place? On Election Day, voters must generally cast a ballot at their assigned polling location. During early voting, voters may use any authorized early voting location within their county. What should I bring? Voters should bring a valid photo ID with a signature. Those who arrive without acceptable identification may be eligible to cast a provisional ballot.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie tests new water sensors as weekend rain threatens flood-prone areas - WFLX
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie tests new water sensors as weekend rain threatens flood-prone areas    WFLX
entry.article_text: More rain is expected this weekend across South Florida and the Treasure Coast, and WPTV is learning that Port St. Lucie Public Works is preparing. Scott Samples, communications manager with the City of Port St. Lucie, said crews spent the week clearing debris from drains and grates. Lucie prepares for rain, flooding concerns Samples added that water levels in retention ponds and canals are at an adequate level and won't need to be lowered. Staff have also been testing their new pilot water sensors, which will send alerts to select staff if water levels rise. "It's a way for us to respond faster to very specific locations," Samples said. Jennifer Collins, owner of Pets Play Grooming off California and Savona boulevards, said her staff is preparing too. "We're nervous about this storm coming up this week," Collins said. "Every time it rains, we get scared." Collins is no stranger to flooding on California and Savona boulevards. She said flooding has occurred there for years. WPTV was there when water levels rose at the intersection last week. Collins said she already sent messages to her customers for Saturday. "We may have to reschedule their dogs. We may have to push them off to next week," Collins said. "Saturdays are one of our busiest days, so it does really affect us as a small business." For long-term solutions at the intersection, the city is working on a large-scale drainage project for the Oak Hammock neighborhood, which includes raising portions of the roadway. "When this project is completed, those problems won't be problems anymore," Samples said. The drainage project is still in data collection before moving on to design. "We can't work if it's raining, and that's in Florida," Collins said. "That's just not OK." The project may take years until completion, but Collins said she already thought about moving her business. "We've also talked about possibly moving, and you know that would be hard too," Collins said. "I just feel like it's not, not getting better."

entry.title: No Kings protests bring demonstrators to streets across Palm Beach County, Treasure Coast - WPEC
entry.summary: No Kings protests bring demonstrators to streets across Palm Beach County, Treasure Coast    WPEC
entry.article_text: Signs reading Dump Trump and Trump for Prison rose above a crowd along Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard on Saturday as music played and demonstrators gathered to voice their opposition. Some wore Resist shirts and shirts featuring comedian Stephen Colbert. In a video posted by Palm Beach Indivisibles, a demonstrator sang songs touching on political and social issues into a microphone, drawing a chorus of Free speech chants when a West Palm Beach police officer attempted to stop her. The chanting continued until the officer left. The gathering near Target was one of several No Kings events scheduled across Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast, as Trump returned to Palm Beach for his first visit of the season. For those who came out, the reasons varied, but several protesters interviewed by Palm Beach Indivisibles described a desire for change. See also: President Trump departs Palm Beach for Kentucky rally after Mar-a-Lago RNC fundraiser We don't have enough time to list all the reasons, but mainly we just need to take our country back and make sure that we have love and kindness and compassion in our hearts again, one demonstrator said. Saturday’s demonstrations were part of a nationwide No Kings: Vote Early day of action. Organizers said more than 3,000 events were planned across the country, with a focus on encouraging voter participation ahead of the Nov. entry.summary: Man dies by suicide after barricaded-subject SWAT situation in Fort Pierce    WPEC
entry.article_text: A man was found dead from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound after deputies responded to a reported domestic violence incident Saturday morning in Fort Pierce's Lakewood Park neighborhood. Deputies responded around 10:17 a.m. to a home in the 7600 block of Winter Garden Boulevard, where they encountered a man in the front yard. The man went back inside after seeing law enforcement, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office . Deputies say they later contacted a man and woman at the front door. A deputy saw what appeared to be a firearm in the man's possession and ordered him to drop the weapon, but he shut the door and retreated inside, prompting a barricaded-subject situation with other occupants still in the home. See also: Driver tried to ram deputy before PIT maneuver ended chase, SLCSO says During the incident, the man reportedly came outside several times and indicated he would surrender after making a phone call, but repeatedly went back inside, deputies said. During his final retreat into the home, deputies say they heard what appeared to be a gunshot. Concerned for an adult woman and children who remained inside, deputies entered the home without alerting the occupants and evacuated them through a side window, according to the sheriff's office. Deputies later found the man dead from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound. The sheriff's office said there is no ongoing threat to the community. Detectives with the agency's Criminal Investigations Division, crime scene technicians and investigators from the Medical Examiner's Office remained at the scene to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident. If you or someone you know is struggling with thoughts of suicide, help is available. Call or text 988 to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline , available 24/7. You can also chat at 988lifeline.org

entry.title: Protesters gather across Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast ahead of midterms - WPBF
entry.summary: Protesters gather across Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast ahead of midterms    WPBF
entry.article_text: Hundreds of residents across the Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast gathered this weekend for "No Kings" protests, urging civic engagement and opposing President Donald Trump’s policies ahead of the midterm elections. Anita Smith, a protester, said, "I am really fed up with the way the institution our government is running." Roger Lyle, another protester, said, "I'm out here to protest the president of the United States because the man is a criminal and he needs to be accounted for." Despite the rain, the protests drew large crowds, with organizers emphasizing the importance of ensuring voters have a plan for the midterms. Just do a little research on what these people have done that want to get into the office, and what do you think they're going to do for you?" Lyle said. Smith added, "Nationwide, it's important because our democracy is turning into fascism and authoritarianism, and we have to correct that." The "No Kings" movement opposes the policies and actions of Trump. On Saturday, protests were planned from the Treasure Coast to southern Palm Beach County. Smith drove from Okeechobee to Port St. Lucie to protest against the current administration and Amendment 3 on property taxes. "Somebody in the fine print is going to get rich off this proposition and nobody is reading the whole thing because it's in legalese and I'm afraid people are going to just vote for it and they don't really know what they're voting for. They think they're going to get money back," Smith said. There were no counterprotesters at the rally. Early voting in the area begins Monday.

entry.title: How to find your polling place in Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast
entry.summary: Before heading to the polls for Florida's 2026 general election, voters should confirm where they are assigned to vote. Polling places can change between election cycles, and election officials recommend checking your polling location well before Election Day. Voters in Palm Beach County, St. Lucie County, Martin County, Indian River County and Okeechobee County can visit their local supervisor of elections website to verify registration information, view their sample ballot and locate their assigned polling place. How do I find my polling place? Most county election offices offer online voter lookup tools that allow voters to: Verify voter registration status View a sample ballot Find their precinct Locate their Election Day polling site Confirm district assignments Can I vote at any polling place? On Election Day, voters must generally cast a ballot at their assigned polling location. During early voting, voters may use any authorized early voting location within their county. What should I bring? Voters should bring a valid photo ID with a signature. Those who arrive without acceptable identification may be eligible to cast a provisional ballot.

entry.title: No Kings protests bring demonstrators to streets across Palm Beach County, Treasure Coast - WPEC
entry.summary: No Kings protests bring demonstrators to streets across Palm Beach County, Treasure Coast    WPEC
entry.article_text: Signs reading Dump Trump and Trump for Prison rose above a crowd along Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard on Saturday as music played and demonstrators gathered to voice their opposition. Some wore Resist shirts and shirts featuring comedian Stephen Colbert. In a video posted by Palm Beach Indivisibles, a demonstrator sang songs touching on political and social issues into a microphone, drawing a chorus of Free speech chants when a West Palm Beach police officer attempted to stop her. The chanting continued until the officer left. The gathering near Target was one of several No Kings events scheduled across Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast, as Trump returned to Palm Beach for his first visit of the season. For those who came out, the reasons varied, but several protesters interviewed by Palm Beach Indivisibles described a desire for change. See also: President Trump departs Palm Beach for Kentucky rally after Mar-a-Lago RNC fundraiser We don't have enough time to list all the reasons, but mainly we just need to take our country back and make sure that we have love and kindness and compassion in our hearts again, one demonstrator said. Another said they were there to oust Trump. A different attendee joked that former President Barack Obama had called and asked him to show up. Saturday’s demonstrations were part of a nationwide No Kings: Vote Early day of action. Organizers said more than 3,000 events were planned across the country, with a focus on encouraging voter participation ahead of the Nov. The effort marks an added focus for the coalition, which has organized demonstrations against what it describes as an expansion of presidential power. This time, organizers are also encouraging people to check their voter registration, learn about their voting options and make a plan to cast a ballot. They describe the voter outreach as nonpartisan. Where No Kings events were scheduled locally Palm Beach County Palm Beach Gardens: 10 a.m. to noon at PGA Boulevard and Campus Drive. on Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard, east of I-95, between Executive Center Drive and Congress Avenue. Wellington: 12:30 to 1:30 p.m. on the public sidewalk in front of the Veterans Memorial. Boynton Beach: 1 to 3 p.m. at Boynton Beach Boulevard and North Congress Avenue. to noon at Boca Raton City Hall. Treasure Coast Sebastian: 10 to 11 a.m. The address was private, with details available through registration. 1 and Kanner Highway/Colorado Avenue. at the MidFlorida Event Center. Protests coincide with Trump's Palm Beach visit President Trump arrived at Donald J. Trump International Airport shortly after 8 p.m. Friday after a rally in Dalton, Georgia. He left Saturday morning for a rally in Kentucky. His visit brought additional security measures and traffic impacts to Palm Beach. South Ocean Boulevard was closed between South County Road and Southern Boulevard, according to the Town of Palm Beach, which advised drivers heading to the island to use the middle or north bridge. The demonstrations came just days before Palm Beach County’s early voting period begins Oct. Voting is scheduled to continue through Nov. 1, ahead of Election Day on Nov.

entry.title: Early voting begins in Palm Beach County, Treasure Coast ahead of 2026 general election - WPEC
entry.summary: Early voting begins in Palm Beach County, Treasure Coast ahead of 2026 general election    WPEC
entry.article_text: Early voting begins Monday across Palm Beach County and parts of the Treasure Coast, giving voters an opportunity to cast their ballots ahead of the Nov. The start of early voting comes after a weekend of No Kings protests across South Florida, where organizers encouraged voter participation and urged residents to make a plan to vote early. The demonstrations, held Saturday in communities including West Palm Beach and Palm Beach Gardens, were part of a nationwide movement protesting President Donald Trump and his administration. This weekend’s events placed an additional focus on voter turnout ahead of the 2026 general elections. When and where can you vote early? Early voting schedules vary by county, with some polling locations opening Monday and others later in the week. There are 28 early voting locations. An additional day of early voting is available Nov. to 4 p.m., with extended hours until 6 p.m. Eligible voters can cast their ballots at any designated early voting location within the county where they are registered. Voters should bring a valid photo ID with a signature. Those without acceptable identification may still cast a provisional ballot. In Palm Beach County, voters can check polling location wait times online and use an optional appointment program to schedule their check-in time. Important election deadlines: The deadline to register to vote in the general election was Oct. Voters planning to cast a ballot by mail have until Thursday, Oct. to request that a ballot be mailed to them. Completed vote-by-mail ballots must be received by election officials no later than 7 p.m. In Palm Beach County, ballots returned to a branch office or secure ballot intake station must arrive by 5 p.m. Election Day polling locations will be open from 7 a.m. Find your early voting location: Voters can find polling locations, county-specific hours and additional election information through their local supervisor of elections: Palm Beach County : VotePalmBeach.gov St. Lucie County: StLucieVotes.gov Martin County: MartinVotes.gov Indian River County: VoteIndianRiver.gov Okeechobee County: VoteOkeechobee.gov

entry.summary: Strong winds, dangerous surf hit Treasure Coast, Palm Beaches    WPBF
entry.article_text: Impact weather is creating hazardous conditions across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beaches on Sunday. A wind advisory is in effect for parts of Indian River County, with sustained winds of 20 to 25 miles per hour and gusts up to 40 miles per hour. Wind gusts around 30 miles per hour have already been recorded this Sunday morning from Sebastian and Vero Beach south through Jupiter, West Palm Beach, Boynton Beach and Boca Raton. Meanwhile, a high surf advisory remains in effect along the Atlantic coast, where seas are expected to reach seven to 12 feet. The rough surf is creating dangerous swimming conditions, a high risk of rip currents and the potential for beach erosion. Forecasters are also monitoring an area in the Atlantic with a 30% chance of tropical development over the next seven days, though no immediate impacts to Florida are expected. Residents are urged to secure loose outdoor items, use caution on the roads and stay out of rough ocean waters.

entry.title: Do seatbelts put students at risk in a school bus rollover? An NTSB expert weighs in
entry.summary: A deadly school bus crash in Polk County is raising new questions about how students are protected when a bus rolls over, including whether wearing a seat belt could create an additional danger. WATCH: AN NTSB EXPERT WEIGHS IN ON SCHOOL BUS SEAT BELTS NTSB on school buses seat belt safety Two weeks after the crash, investigative reporter Katie LaGrone put that question directly to Dr. Kristin Poland, a school bus safety expert with the National Transportation Safety Board . The crash killed 16-year-old Adinaluz Prieto Oyola during the morning commute on Oct. 5. According to investigators, the school bus carrying 37 high school students was on its way to Winter Haven High School when another cut slammed into its rear, causing the bus to collide head-on with another vehicle and flip over. Following the crash, Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd was asked whether any of the dozens of students aboard were wearing seat belts at the time of impact. 'Quite frankly, if you try to make everyone put a seat belt on, then we would have had 37 kids hanging from the roof by a seat belt,' Judd said. His comments raise a key safety question: In a rollover crash, do seat belts protect students or potentially put them at greater risk? While Poland said the NTSB cannot yet discuss specifics of its investigation into the Polk County crash, she pointed to what the agency has learned from other school bus crashes. 'The real risk is when theyre violently thrown during the crash sequence about the inside of the bus, where they hit other occupants, or they could potentially hit hard points inside the school bus,' Poland said. According to Poland, properly worn three-point restraints, which include both a lap and shoulder belt, provide the best protection even when a bus overturns. 'Those seat belts are designed so that students can still release the belts even if they're under tension, like if a student is hanging from the belt,' she said. Poland acknowledged that the image of a child hanging by a seat belt after a rollover may sound frightening. But she said the greater danger comes during the crash itself, when an unrestrained student can be thrown around the bus. The NTSB has not determined whether a three-point seat belt could have changed the outcome of the Polk County crash. The school district confirmed the bus involved was only equipped with lap belts as are all the school buses in its fleet, according to a district spokesperson. A safety issue investigated for years For report

But she said the greater danger comes during the crash itself, when an unrestrained student can be thrown around the bus.The NTSB has not determined whether a three-point seat belt could have changed the outcome of the Polk County crash. The school district confirmed the bus involved was only equipped with lap belts as are all the school buses in its fleet, according to a district spokesperson.A safety issue investigated for yearsFor reporter LaGrone, the questions surrounding school bus restraints aren't new. More than a decade ago, she investigated a St. Lucie County school bus crash that killed 9-year-old Aaron Beauchamp, who was wearing a lap belt at the time.The NTSB investigated that crash and produced simulations demonstrating the difference between the protection provided by a lap belt and the protection provided when a shoulder belt is added.A few years later, the agency formally recommended that school districts in the U.S. upgrade school bus restraints to include both lap and shoulder belts. Florida was among the states called on to make three-point seat belts state law.What does Florida require?Currently, Florida only requires school buses to be equipped with lap belts, but students are not required to wear them.Nearly a decade after the NTSB's recommendation, Poland said some Florida school districts are moving toward three-point lap-and-shoulder belts. “We're seeing some progress with some of the school districts in Florida moving to the passenger lap shoulder belts,” she said.But our investigation found that the majority of public school buses in the state still have lap belts only.Cost is one hurdle. Still, Poland said installing the equipment is only part of improving student safety. "It's not enough just to have the lap shoulder belts on the bus, there also has to be an entire layered approach to ensure that the students are wearing the belts properly," she said. That approach also requires involvement and oversight from school districts and parents, Poland said.But Poland wants to emphasize that school buses remain the safest mode of transportation for students traveling to and from school, regardless of what kind of seat belts are on board. For Poland, seat belt use on school buses is a major step toward the agency's ultimate goal. "We think we can get to zero fatalities in school buses and that's what we're looking towards," Poland said.

entry.title: Ballet Palm Beach brings Mary Shelley's 'Frankenstein' to the Kravis Center in West Palm Beach
entry.summary: Ballet Palm Beach is bringing one of literature's most iconic stories to the stage this month with its original production of Mary Shelley's Frankenstein at the Kravis Center in West Palm Beach. The production runs Oct. 22 through Oct. 24 at the Marshall E. Rinker Sr. Playhouse and reimagines Mary Shelley's classic novel through contemporary ballet. Ballet Palm Beach describes the performance as a dramatic exploration of ambition, abandonment and identity. The company is the professional ballet company of Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast. WATCH BELOW: Ballet Palm Beach brings 'Frankenstein' to the Kravis Center Inside Ballet Palm Beach's world-premiere Frankenstein According to Founding Artistic and Executive Director Colleen Smith, the story begins before Frankenstein's monster ever comes to life. 'It's a gorgeous production about Mary Shelley and her haunting book Frankenstein,' Smith said. During the broadcast, Smith explained how the famous story was born during a gathering at Lake Geneva. 'They were gathered together on the shores of Lake Geneva on a stormy night, and Lord Byron was reading ghost stories and said, 'You know what, guys, let's create our own ghost stories,' and she did,' Smith said. 'First science fiction novel ever written by an 18-year-old woman.' Dancer Leah Walker said audiences can expect something different from a traditional ballet. 'Most classical ballets are fantasy, but ours does follow the real story of Mary Shelley and her process as she writes it,' Leah said. 'It's a horror. It's a very contemporary, very artistic take.' The production is recommended for ages 9 and older and features two 45-minute acts separated by a 20-minute intermission. For audiences looking for a Halloween-season experience with a local arts connection, the performance offers a fresh take on a familiar tale. The production combines historical elements from Mary Shelley's life with the themes that have made Frankenstein one of the most enduring stories ever written. Tickets and performance information are available through Ballet Palm Beach and the Kravis Center. entry.title: Bomb threat prompts heavy law enforcement response near Trump airport in Palm Beach County
entry.summary: A bomb threat near Donald J. entry.title: Palm Beach County 'No Kings' rally urges early voting

entry.title: Man found dead after barricade situation in St. Lucie County, deputies say
entry.summary: A man was found dead from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound Saturday after a barricade situation prompted deputies to evacuate a woman and children from a St. Lucie County home, according to the sheriffs office. The St. Lucie County Sheriffs Office said deputies responded around 10:17 a.m. to a reported domestic violence incident in the 7600 block of Winter Garden Boulevard. WATCH BELOW: Man found dead after St. Lucie County barricade situation Man found dead after barricade situation in St. Lucie County Deputies initially encountered a man in the front yard who went back inside after seeing law enforcement. Authorities later made contact with a man and woman at the front door. During that interaction, a deputy saw what appeared to be a firearm in the man's possession and ordered him to drop it, the sheriffs office said. Instead, the man closed the door and retreated inside, creating a barricaded-subject situation while other people remained in the home. According to investigators, the man came outside several times and said he would surrender after making a phone call, but repeatedly went back inside. During his final retreat into the home, deputies heard what appeared to be a gunshot. Knowing a woman and children were still inside and could be in danger, deputies entered the residence and evacuated them through a side window, the sheriffs office said. Deputies later found the man dead from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound. Authorities said there is no ongoing threat to the community. Detectives, crime scene technicians and investigators from the Medical Examiners Office are expected to remain at the scene for several hours as the investigation continues.

entry.summary: Baseball Hall of Famer Andre Dawson received the Governors Medal of Freedom. Governor Ron DeSantis said the award recognizes Dawsons baseball career, his contributions to Florida AM University, and his lasting impact on the state of Florida. Dawson was born in Miami and went to Southwest Miami Senior High School. He then went to Florida AM and walked on to the Rattlers baseball team. His performance led the Montreal Expos to select him in the 1975 MLB draft. His distinguished career in Major League Baseball, his contributions to the sport, and his lasting impact on our state have earned him this award. The Hawk has represented Florida in the best possible way for decades. His generous support of FAMU and its baseball program has helped generations of student-athletes succeed. The Governors Medal of Freedom is the highest honor I can bestow on any Floridian, and Andre Dawson truly deserves this recognition, DeSantis said. Past recipients of the Governors Medal of Freedom include Florida State University football coach Bobby Bowden, golfer Barbara Nicklaus, musician Jimmy Buffett, Coach Lee Corso, and former Florida Supreme Court Justice Charles Canady. entry.title: Florida secures arrest warrant for Raúl Castro in 1996 Brothers to the Rescue shootdown
entry.summary: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier announced Monday that state prosecutors and the Florida Department of Law Enforcement (FDLE) have secured an arrest warrant for former Cuban leader Ral Castro, accusing him of conspiring to murder four men in the 1996 shootdown of two civilian aircraft operated by the anti-Castro group Brothers to the Rescue. According to the Attorney General's Office, Castro has been charged with one count of conspiracy to commit first-degree murder in connection with an incident in which Cuban military fighter jets shot down two unarmed Brothers to the Rescue planes over international waters. Authorities said three unarmed Cessna aircraft departed Opa-locka Airport in Miami-Dade County on Feb. 24, 1996. After crossing the 24th parallel and flying outside Cuba's territorial waters, two of the planes were destroyed by air-to-air missiles fired by Cuban MiG fighter jets. According to the affidavit, the aircraft were traveling away from Cuba at the time and received no warning before being shot down. The warrant, obtained by the Office of Statewide Prosecution and FDLE, alleges Castro played a key role in authorizing the attack that killed four men with ties to Florida: Carlos Costa, Pablo Morales, Mario de la Pea and Armando Alejandre Jr. 'Ral Castro ordered the murder of four Floridians in cold blood, and Florida will never stop pursuing accountability for that communist conspiracy,' Uthmeier said in a statement. According to a probable cause affidavit, Castro, who at the time served as Cuba's minister of the Revolutionary Armed Forces and first vice president, was among the final decision-makers who authorized the operation. Investigators allege Castro issued standing orders to military leaders to shoot down aircraft associated with Brothers to the Rescue if they appeared over the sea. State investigators also allege Cuban intelligence agents operating in South Florida infiltrated Brothers to the Rescue and provided flight information to the Cuban government as part of what was known as 'Operation Scorpion.' Miami-Dade Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz called the warrant a 'historic step toward accountability' for the four men killed in the attack, while FDLE Special Agent in Charge Michael Stein said the case demonstrates that 'the passage of time does not diminish the pursuit of justice.' The warrant charges Castro under Florida statutes governing conspiracy and first-degree murder. Prosecutors said the offense is a first-degree felony,

entry.title: Man convicted of killing Indian River County deputy set for execution Tuesday - WPEC
entry.summary: Man convicted of killing Indian River County deputy set for execution Tuesday    WPEC
entry.article_text: The man convicted of killing an Indian River County deputy nearly 40 years ago is scheduled to be executed Tuesday. William Reaves, 77, is set to die by lethal injection at 6 p.m. at Florida State Prison near Starke . Ron DeSantis signed the death warrant Sept. According to court records, Cpl. Richard Raczkoski was called to a Zippy Mart near Vero Beach around 3 a.m. 23, 1986, to help Reaves get a cab. During the encounter, a gun fell from Reaves’ shorts and the two struggled over it. Records say Reaves shot the deputy four times in the back. In a taped interview with Indian River County detectives in Albany, Reaves admitted to the shooting. I’ve never met a finer officer in my life, he said, according to a transcript filed by the state. When a detective asked why he would not give up the gun, Reaves said he was a convicted felon and feared prison. I know if I got caught with that gun, and the man take me down there, I’m gonna get a mandatory three years already for the gun, he said. Reaves also told detectives, I was all coked up and I panicked, both of us panicked. Prosecutors have long argued the shooting was premeditated. Court records show the deputy was running away when he was shot, and the .380 handgun required a separate trigger pull for each shot. See also: Florida secures state arrest warrant for Raúl Castro in 1996 shootdown Reaves was convicted and sentenced to death. The Florida Supreme Court rejected his latest appeals last week, and a request for the U.S. Supreme Court to review his case is still pending. His attorneys and supporters, including a group of military veterans, have asked DeSantis to spare his life, pointing to his service in Vietnam. Reaves was first convicted in 1987, but the Florida Supreme Court threw out that conviction in 1991 because one of the prosecutors had previously represented Reaves in another case. A second jury convicted him again in 1992 and voted 10-2 to recommend the death penalty. In a court filing last month, Reaves’ attorneys said he was deployed to Vietnam as a ground combat soldier in 1969, at age 20. They say the Department of Veterans Affairs rates him 100% disabled for post-traumatic stress disorder, and that the jury that sentenced him never heard the details of his combat service. His attorneys also argued that Reaves was shut out of the clemency process. They said the attorney assigned to represent him met with him about five minutes before his clemency interview and never gave him a copy of what was submitted on his behalf. A circuit judge ruled Reaves received a full clemency proceeding. The governor denied clemency the same day he signed the death warrant. In the same filing, the defense accused two former Indian River County deputies of taking bribes from a drug dealer in the 1980s. The defense also said one of them helped shape the testimony of a key witness against Reaves. Circuit Judge Anastasia Norman rejected the claim on Oct. 2, finding the allegations were not backed by any sworn statement and were merely speculative at best. Reaves did not raise that claim in his appeal to the Florida Supreme Court. Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers, who pushed for the governor to sign the warrant, describes the moment when he learned the governor signed Reaves' death warrant. "It was not something that I had expected. At this point, our governor is wrapping things up in Tallahassee and finishing out his time. So for him to take time to make sure that this gets handled is just really a blessing," said Flowers. Flowers plans to attend the execution in Raiford on Tuesday. My goal with going tomorrow is ultimately the last thing that he sees is an Indian River County Sheriff’s Office uniform, knowing that justice finally came, Flowers said. Flowers said Raczkoski’s brother will also be there. Raczkoski’s parents have since died. Flowers said the brother told him, Christmas was never the same for our family after Richard was killed. The execution comes nearly a year after the agency lost Sgt. Terri Sweeting-Mashkow, who was killed in the line of duty in November 2025. Flowers said Tuesday will bring the agency some closure. It just really feels like coming full circle, like a moment of healing that we all needed, Flowers said. Supreme Court appeal still pending, Flowers said he will not rest easy until the execution is carried out. I’d hate to see it delayed in any way, he said.

Kyle Kennedy was arrested Friday after an investigation by the Fort Pierce Police Department into multiple reports of indecent exposure on the bridge. Investigators reviewed previous reports and spotted patterns linking the incidents, then interviewed victims and conducted photo lineups, police said. entry.title: Man found dead after barricade situation in St. Lucie County, deputies say
entry.summary: A man was found dead from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound Saturday after a barricade situation prompted deputies to evacuate a woman and children from a St. Lucie County home, according to the sheriffs office. The St. Lucie County Sheriffs Office said deputies responded around 10:17 a.m. to a reported domestic violence incident in the 7600 block of Winter Garden Boulevard. WATCH BELOW: Man found dead after St. Lucie County barricade situation Man found dead after barricade situation in St. Lucie County Deputies initially encountered a man in the front yard who went back inside after seeing law enforcement. Authorities later made contact with a man and woman at the front door. During that interaction, a deputy saw what appeared to be a firearm in the man's possession and ordered him to drop it, the sheriffs office said. Instead, the man closed the door and retreated inside, creating a barricaded-subject situation while other people remained in the home. According to investigators, the man came outside several times and said he would surrender after making a phone call, but repeatedly went back inside. During his final retreat into the home, deputies heard what appeared to be a gunshot. Knowing a woman and children were still inside and could be in danger, deputies entered the residence and evacuated them through a side window, the sheriffs office said. Deputies later found the man dead from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound. Authorities said there is no ongoing threat to the community. Detectives, crime scene technicians and investigators from the Medical Examiners Office are expected to remain at the scene for several hours as the investigation continues.

entry.title: Do seatbelts put students at risk in a school bus rollover? An NTSB expert weighs in
entry.summary: A deadly school bus crash in Polk County is raising new questions about how students are protected when a bus rolls over, including whether wearing a seat belt could create an additional danger. WATCH: AN NTSB EXPERT WEIGHS IN ON SCHOOL BUS SEAT BELTS NTSB on school buses seat belt safety Two weeks after the crash, investigative reporter Katie LaGrone put that question directly to Dr. Kristin Poland, a school bus safety expert with the National Transportation Safety Board . The crash killed 16-year-old Adinaluz Prieto Oyola during the morning commute on Oct. 5. According to investigators, the school bus carrying 37 high school students was on its way to Winter Haven High School when another cut slammed into its rear, causing the bus to collide head-on with another vehicle and flip over. Following the crash, Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd was asked whether any of the dozens of students aboard were wearing seat belts at the time of impact. 'Quite frankly, if you try to make everyone put a seat belt on, then we would have had 37 kids hanging from the roof by a seat belt,' Judd said. His comments raise a key safety question: In a rollover crash, do seat belts protect students or potentially put them at greater risk? While Poland said the NTSB cannot yet discuss specifics of its investigation into the Polk County crash, she pointed to what the agency has learned from other school bus crashes. 'The real risk is when theyre violently thrown during the crash sequence about the inside of the bus, where they hit other occupants, or they could potentially hit hard points inside the school bus,' Poland said. According to Poland, properly worn three-point restraints, which include both a lap and shoulder belt, provide the best protection even when a bus overturns. 'Those seat belts are designed so that students can still release the belts even if they're under tension, like if a student is hanging from the belt,' she said. Poland acknowledged that the image of a child hanging by a seat belt after a rollover may sound frightening. But she said the greater danger comes during the crash itself, when an unrestrained student can be thrown around the bus. The NTSB has not determined whether a three-point seat belt could have changed the outcome of the Polk County crash. The school district confirmed the bus involved was only equipped with lap belts as are all the school buses in its fleet, according to a district spokesperson. A safety issue investigated for years For report

More than a decade ago, she investigated a St. Lucie County school bus crash that killed 9-year-old Aaron Beauchamp, who was wearing a lap belt at the time.The NTSB investigated that crash and produced simulations demonstrating the difference between the protection provided by a lap belt and the protection provided when a shoulder belt is added.A few years later, the agency formally recommended that school districts in the U.S. upgrade school bus restraints to include both lap and shoulder belts. Florida was among the states called on to make three-point seat belts state law.What does Florida require?Currently, Florida only requires school buses to be equipped with lap belts, but students are not required to wear them.Nearly a decade after the NTSB's recommendation, Poland said some Florida school districts are moving toward three-point lap-and-shoulder belts. “We're seeing some progress with some of the school districts in Florida moving to the passenger lap shoulder belts,” she said.But our investigation found that the majority of public school buses in the state still have lap belts only.Cost is one hurdle. Still, Poland said installing the equipment is only part of improving student safety. "It's not enough just to have the lap shoulder belts on the bus, there also has to be an entire layered approach to ensure that the students are wearing the belts properly," she said. That approach also requires involvement and oversight from school districts and parents, Poland said.But Poland wants to emphasize that school buses remain the safest mode of transportation for students traveling to and from school, regardless of what kind of seat belts are on board. For Poland, seat belt use on school buses is a major step toward the agency's ultimate goal. "We think we can get to zero fatalities in school buses and that's what we're looking towards," Poland said.

entry.article_text: A Vero Beach man accused of restraining a woman in a hotel room and throwing water on her after she tried to leave has been sentenced to nine months in jail. Frank Joseph Lagola pleaded no contest to charges of false imprisonment and battery and was sentenced Thursday, according to court records. Deputies with the Indian River County Sheriff's Office say they were called to Econo Lodge at 950 U.S. Highway 1 in Vero Beach on December 23, 2025, after a witness reported hearing a woman screaming for help. The witness told deputies she saw a man restraining a woman in the hotel doorway, preventing her from leaving. See also: Fort Pierce flasher? Coppeto told deputies she had been staying at the hotel for about a week and wanted to leave the room. She alleged Lagola became increasingly agitated, threw "holy" water on her, and physically restrained her, telling her she wasn't going anywhere. According to the affidavit, Coppeto said Lagola pinned her down and struck her on the top of her head. She also told deputies she screamed for help because she did not have a cellphone and could not physically get away from him. Lagola told deputies he believed Coppeto was possessed by the devil after she began speaking in Latin. He said he was trying to perform an exorcism and admitted holding her down while reading Bible passages, according to the affidavit. Investigators also spoke with a witness who said she heard a woman yelling, Stop, Rape, Help Me, before seeing the man appear to drag the woman back into the room. entry.title: Miami native and baseball Hall of Famer Andre Dawson receives the Governors Medal of Freedom
entry.summary: Baseball Hall of Famer Andre Dawson received the Governors Medal of Freedom. Gov. Ron DeSantis said the award recognizes Dawson's baseball career, his contributions to Florida AM University, and his lasting impact on the state of Florida. Dawson was born in Miami and went to Southwest Miami Senior High School. He then went to Florida AM and walked on to the Rattlers baseball team. His performance led the Montreal Expos to select him in the 1975 MLB draft. His distinguished career in Major League Baseball, his contributions to the sport, and his lasting impact on our state have earned him this award. 'The Hawk' has represented Florida in the best possible way for decades. His generous support of FAMU and its baseball program has helped generations of student-athletes succeed. The Governors Medal of Freedom is the highest honor I can bestow on any Floridian, and Andre Dawson truly deserves this recognition, DeSantis said. Past recipients of the Governors Medal of Freedom include Florida State University football coach Bobby Bowden, golfer Barbara Nicklaus, musician Jimmy Buffett, Coach Lee Corso, and former Florida Supreme Court Justice Charles Canady.

entry.summary: Man dies by suicide after barricaded-subject SWAT situation in Fort Pierce    cw34.com
entry.article_text: A man was found dead from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound after deputies responded to a reported domestic violence incident Saturday morning in Fort Pierce's Lakewood Park neighborhood. Deputies responded around 10:17 a.m. to a home in the 7600 block of Winter Garden Boulevard, where they encountered a man in the front yard. The man went back inside after seeing law enforcement, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office . Deputies say they later contacted a man and woman at the front door. A deputy saw what appeared to be a firearm in the man's possession and ordered him to drop the weapon, but he shut the door and retreated inside, prompting a barricaded-subject situation with other occupants still in the home. See also: Driver tried to ram deputy before PIT maneuver ended chase, SLCSO says During the incident, the man reportedly came outside several times and indicated he would surrender after making a phone call, but repeatedly went back inside, deputies said. During his final retreat into the home, deputies say they heard what appeared to be a gunshot. Concerned for an adult woman and children who remained inside, deputies entered the home without alerting the occupants and evacuated them through a side window, according to the sheriff's office. Deputies later found the man dead from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound. The sheriff's office said there is no ongoing threat to the community. Detectives with the agency's Criminal Investigations Division, crime scene technicians and investigators from the Medical Examiner's Office remained at the scene to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident. If you or someone you know is struggling with thoughts of suicide, help is available. Call or text 988 to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline , available 24/7. You can also chat at 988lifeline.org

entry.title: Lake Worth Beach food-sharing ordinance sparks new dispute over weekly Bryant Park gatherings
entry.summary: A weekly community gathering at Bryant Park is drawing renewed scrutiny in Lake Worth Beach as organizers question how the city is enforcing a new ordinance regulating food-sharing events in public parks. Melissa Salerno, a community member involved in the weekly gatherings, says the group continues to meet to share food and spend time together. WATCH WPTV'S COVERAGE BELOW: This is a picnic: Bryant Park organizers push back on Lake Worth Beach Ordinance But she says members have repeatedly been told by law enforcement that they are violating the city's rules, even as organizers maintain they are keeping attendance below 25 people and gathering for a picnic rather than a food distribution event. The dispute centers on how the city defines a food-sharing event, which rules apply to smaller gatherings, and why Bryant Park is excluded from the locations where these events are permitted. During a recent gathering, attendance appeared significantly lower than at previous events. Legal observers were also present after organizers invited them to monitor the gathering in case tensions escalated, equipped with body cameras and a measuring tape to comply with Florida's Halo law. 'According to the city, this is a food distribution event, and we are therefore in violation of the ordinance,' Salerno said. 'And what I tried to clarify was that this is not a food distribution event; this is a picnic.' Salerno said the group wants to continue gathering without feeling intimidated or monitored. entry.article_text: A weekly community gathering at Bryant Park is drawing renewed scrutiny in Lake Worth Beach as organizers question how the city is enforcing a new ordinance regulating food-sharing events in public parks.Melissa Salerno, a community member involved in the weekly gatherings, says the group continues to meet to share food and spend time together. WATCH WPTV'S COVERAGE BELOW: But she says members have repeatedly been told by law enforcement that they are violating the city's rules, even as organizers maintain they are keeping attendance below 25 people and gathering for a picnic rather than a food distribution event.The dispute centers on how the city defines a food-sharing event, which rules apply to smaller gatherings, and why Bryant Park is excluded from the locations where these events are permitted.During a recent gathering, attendance appeared significantly lower than at previous events. Legal observers were also present after organizers invited them to monitor the gathering in case tensions escalated, equipped with body cameras and a measuring tape to comply with Florida's Halo law. Rick White, one of the legal observers, said their role was to help ensure participants' rights were respected."Just to make sure no one's civil rights are being violated, either way we're neutral; we're not here for one side or the other," White said.Salerno said organizers have attempted to follow the new ordinance by keeping participation below 25 people. She also disputes the city's characterization of the gathering as a food distribution event."According to the city, this is a food distribution event, and we are therefore in violation of the ordinance," Salerno said. "And what I tried to clarify was that this is not a food distribution event; this is a picnic."Salerno said the group wants to continue gathering without feeling intimidated or monitored."We just share each other's company and time,” she said.She also emphasized the importance of transparency and public awareness surrounding the city’s decisions."I think it's really important that the community at large knows what's going on, how their taxpayer dollars are being spent,” Salerno said.The Lake Worth Beach City Commission approved Ordinance 2026-01 on Feb. 3, 2026, tightening requirements for special events on city property, including organized food-sharing events. The measure followed complaints from downtown businesses and visitors about food-sharing gatherings at Bryant Park, including events serving people experiencing homelessness. Under the ordinance, a special event generally includes a gathering that attracts, is intended to attract, or is likely to attract 25 or more people, including staff, vendors and volunteers. The ordinance defines food-sharing events to include social-service food sharing and public events where food is provided or served at no charge in a public space.Those events are restricted to three designated locations:Memorial Park PavilionHoward Park PavilionNorthwest ParkA special-event permit application must be submitted at least 30 days in advance. The ordinance also limits the number of food-sharing event permits issued to the same person, group or organization at the same public space to 12 within a consecutive 12-month period. Additional requirements may include liability insurance, food-safety credentials for certain food preparation and service, and arrangements for cleanup. The restrictions mean that staying below 25 people does not automatically resolve every question about whether a gathering is allowed. Stuart Sword, interim director of Lake Worth Beach’s Leisure Services Department, said Bryant Park is not one of the approved locations for food-sharing events.Sword said the city selected the three designated parks partly because of their proximity to public transportation, making them accessible to people who rely on those services."Anytime there's a food-sharing event, there are significant implications to the park and also waste management,” Sword said.He said the city is trying to manage the impact of these gatherings while preserving public spaces for other uses."We identified three parks where you can do that, Northwest Ball Field, Memorial Park and Howard Park, and the reason the city picked those is 'cause they're close to public transportation," Sword said.Sword acknowledged a distinction between a picnic and a food-sharing event, adding that it's a clarification that would have to be made by the city attorney. WPTV began reporting on the proposal in June 2025, when organizers said they were serving growing numbers of people facing food insecurity amid rising housing costs and inflation. At the time, Salerno said Bryant Park was important because of its central location and access to bus routes. City leaders argued that organized events involving large numbers of people require planning, cleanup and coordination to protect public spaces and ensure other residents can use them.But advocates have argued that the requirements could create financial and logistical barriers for volunteer-led groups that rely on donations and personal contributions to provide meals.For now, the disagreement between organizers and the city remains focused on the ordinance’s application to the weekly Bryant Park gathering.Organizers say they want to continue meeting and sharing meals while complying with the rules. The city maintains that Bryant Park is not an approved location for food-sharing events and says its goal is to keep public spaces safe, clean and accessible.

entry.title: Delray Beach homeowner says insurance went up $300 a year after replacing her roof through state program
entry.summary: Betty Haygood of Delray Beach says she is happy with her new roof after it was installed in August with help from the My Safe Florida Home program. However, what does not make her happy is her homeowners insurance renewal that's due in December. WATCH BELOW: Delray resident says insurance rose $300 after she replaced her roof Delray Beach woman's insurance rose $300 after new roof through state program 'They're saying it's $300,' she told us as we talked in her kitchen on Monday. At 76 years old, an increase like that doesn't come easily for Haygood, so she contacted WPTV looking for some answers. 'I'm upset about it because the simple fact that a person has replaced an old roof, if it doesn't stay where it is, there should be some kind of reduction,' Haygood says. When it comes to homeowners insurance, setting premiums can be complicated. In many cases, rates can go down, and premiums go up, especially during periods of inflation. WPTV contacted Betty's insurance company, Universal, which is based in South Florida. They told us that her old roof was only insured at 25% value because of its age. Now, with a new roof, she has more comprehensive coverage, causing the increase. Insurance experts and state leaders tell us the insurance market in Florida is improving , with more new companies, competition and more pressure to lower rates.

entry.summary: A push from a Pahokee resident at a recent county commission meeting is shining new light on a long-delayed affordable housing development that local leaders say remains badly needed across the Glades. Consuela Cunningham Benjamin traveled to West Palm Beach to urge county leaders to make it a priority to complete the Everglades Townhomes project. I was born and raised in Pahokee, Florida,' Consuela told commissioners. 'I joined the military, served in the Army in hopes of returning home to adequate housing.' She said affordable housing remains difficult to find in the community. The Everglades Townhomes project is expected to bring 60 affordable rental units to Pahokee, but Consuela noted the development has faced years of delays. entry.title: Vero Beach gives Three Corners developers another extension as Dec. 8 deadline looms
entry.summary: WPTV is learning that the Vero Beach City Council approved an extension for developers of the Three Corners project but time is ticking. City council members told the developers, ClearBlue, that they need to negotiate and come to an agreement by Dec. 8 or the city may need to go back to the drawing board. WATCH BELOW: Developers get 4th extension for Three Corners project Developers get fourth extension for negotiations on Three Corners project 'I've been on this thing since 2019,' Vero Beach Mayor John Cotugno said. 'We need to negotiate the best, we'll call it a deal, for our citizens.'  The development project is located at the old Vero Beach Power Plant at the base of the 17th Street Bridge. Plans include hotels, a marina, restaurants, walking paths and more. This is the fourth extension the city council approved for developers to negotiate agreements on financing and lease terms. 'Some progress had been made on the financial aspects of the developer proposal,' Cotugno said. But the mayor said if the council and ClearBlue aren't on the same page, they might have to change course. 'We need to listen and to see if this aligns with our goals and objectives. And if it does, great, we're going to work out a deal that's mutually beneficial,' Cotugno said. 'If not, then you know well we'll have to see what happens.' Cotugno said the city council is also appointing a liaison to aid in negotiations and the developers come to discuss the project in person. Bob Salera, a spokesperson for ClearBlue, said they are meeting with city council Oct. 27. 'It's something that we've actually been asking for for several months,' Salera said. 'We're glad we finally have one on the books now.' Salera said they're committed to the project and have invested over $1 million. 'We wouldn't have put in 21,000 hours of time into this project if we weren't serious,' Salera said. 'We're happy that these negotiations are moving forward, and we're ready to bring it home to a close.' Cotugno said he hopes they do. 'I'm willing to stay at that the table if progress is being made,' Cotugno said.

entry.title: Up to 12-foot waves pound Palm Beach County, Treasure Coast beaches - WPEC
entry.summary: Up to 12-foot waves pound Palm Beach County, Treasure Coast beaches    WPEC
entry.article_text: Waves reaching up to 12 feet are pounding beaches across Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast Monday, drawing experienced surfers into the water while prompting lifeguards in Jupiter to raise double red flags and prohibit swimming. From Boca Raton to Sebastian, beaches are experiencing rough surf and dangerous rip currents, with conditions expected to continue over the next several days. At Jupiter Beach Park Monday, CBS12 News watched surfers battle choppy waves, a kite surfer take advantage of the strong winds and beachgoers enjoy the sunshine from the sand. But lifeguards were taking the conditions seriously. "We're changing our flags from single red to double red, so this entire area is going to be with no swimming," said Ethan Sage, a Jupiter Ocean Rescue lifeguard. Sage said double red flags are typically needed only a few times a year, usually during major storms or unusually rough conditions. He estimated wave faces reaching 12 to 15 feet beyond the sandbars Monday, compared with 4 to 6 feet Sunday. Despite the warnings, some experienced surfers were eager to get into the water. "When it gets this big, I mean, we kind of want to go out there and let the ocean humble us a little bit," said surfer JC Southwell. Southwell said he would rather take on windy, choppy conditions than spend a day watching a flat ocean. Kite surfer Joe Goulet was also excited about the conditions, saying the wind and waves give him an opportunity to challenge himself and improve his skills. "It's a blast," Goulet said. But for other beachgoers, the waves were better enjoyed from a distance. Isis Alize brought her baby to the beach but had no plans to take her swimming. "Definitely a water baby," Alize said of her daughter. "We dipped our toes, and that was a bit scary, actually." What's causing the big waves? CBS12 News meteorologist Lauren Olesky said a nor'easter developing off the East Coast is sending large swells down the coastline. "So, we're dealing with waves breaking up to about 10 to 12 feet," Olesky said. The system developed along the same frontal boundary that brought rain to South Florida late last week and over the weekend. Olesky said high surf advisories extend across the region, with strong onshore winds contributing to the rough conditions. While the waves may be exciting for experienced surfers, Olesky warned that the high risk of rip currents makes swimming especially dangerous. "Even if you are a super strong swimmer, it can get tiring trying to fight the current if you're out there for an extended period of time," she said. Sage warned that even standing close to the water can be dangerous when powerful waves crash onto the shore. See also: 5,543 calls in 13 days: Palm Beach County's trash troubles pile up He said surfers are allowed to enter the water at their own discretion where the Jupiter restrictions are in place, but recommended that only experts consider going out. What beachgoers should know With seasonal visitors beginning to return to South Florida, Olesky encouraged everyone to check the forecast and beach warning flags before heading into the ocean. She recommended swimming only at lifeguarded beaches when conditions allow and paying attention to posted warnings. At the Jupiter beach CBS12 News visited, double red flags mean no swimming. And beachgoers hoping for calmer conditions may have to wait. Olesky said the large waves and high rip current risk are expected to continue over the next several days, giving experienced surfers more opportunities to catch waves while keeping lifeguards on high alert.

entry.title: More than 100 cats rescued from hoarding situation in Port St. Lucie - WPBF
entry.summary: More than 100 cats rescued from hoarding situation in Port St. Lucie    WPBF
entry.article_text: More than 100 cats and kittens rescued from a hoarding situation in Port St. Lucie are now receiving medical care and nourishment at the Humane Society of St. Lucie Animal Control removed the animals over the course of three days last week, with the first group arriving at the shelter on Tuesday. "Some were clearly showing symptoms of upper respiratory. The majority of them had ear mites. They were all covered in fleas. There were a couple that had open sores, from scratching at the flea, scratching at the ear mites and some other issues," said Sarah Wees, executive director of the Humane Society of St. Three pregnant cats gave birth shortly after being rescued, with one too weak to care for her kittens. Those newborns were rushed to an emergency foster home for round-the-clock care, while others remain at the shelter. "We have kittens who are nursing on cats that may or may not be their mom because we really can't tell who belongs with whom because they were all in the same house together," Wees said. The Humane Society is receiving assistance from American Humane, a national organization that supports local communities during large intake cases or natural disasters. "She reached out to me, and by Thursday morning I was on property, and helping just work through those initial days, and also coordinating some volunteers and additional staffing to come in to help with additional personnel," said Taylor Nickelsen, a certified animal responder with American Humane. Nickelsen said their efforts are making a difference, with many of the cats showing significant improvement. "We stay as long as we need to be able to provide the relief that is needed, which ultimately our goal is to help get these animals on their way to foster and on their way to adoption," Nickelsen said. Lucie police are monitoring the case to determine if any criminal charges will be filed. In the meantime, the Humane Society is seeking donations and volunteers to help care for the rescued cats and kittens. entry.summary: Man found dead after barricade situation in St. Lucie County, deputies say    WFLX
entry.article_text: A man was found dead from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound Saturday after a barricade situation prompted deputies to evacuate a woman and children from a St. Lucie County home, according to the sheriff’s office. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office said deputies responded around 10:17 a.m. to a reported domestic violence incident in the 7600 block of Winter Garden Boulevard. WATCH BELOW: Man found dead after St. Lucie County barricade situation Deputies initially encountered a man in the front yard who went back inside after seeing law enforcement. Authorities later made contact with a man and woman at the front door. During that interaction, a deputy saw what appeared to be a firearm in the man's possession and ordered him to drop it, the sheriff’s office said. Instead, the man closed the door and retreated inside, creating a barricaded-subject situation while other people remained in the home. According to investigators, the man came outside several times and said he would surrender after making a phone call, but repeatedly went back inside. During his final retreat into the home, deputies heard what appeared to be a gunshot. Knowing a woman and children were still inside and could be in danger, deputies entered the residence and evacuated them through a side window, the sheriff’s office said. Deputies later found the man dead from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound. Authorities said there is no ongoing threat to the community. Detectives, crime scene technicians and investigators from the Medical Examiner’s Office are expected to remain at the scene for several hours as the investigation continues.

entry.title: Martin County woman honored after using CPR to save 3-year-old girl from swimming pool
entry.summary: A 20-year-old Martin County woman is being honored after she used CPR to help save a 3-year-old girl she found motionless at the bottom of a swimming pool. Nearly two months after the August rescue, Martin County Fire Rescue recognized Madison Isler with the department's Heroic Heart Award. WATCH: Martin County woman honored for saving 3-year-old Woman Honored After Using CPR to Save 3-Year-Old Girl | WPTV The rescue happened Aug. 23 as Isler walked past the pool at her apartment complex. She told WPTV something in the water caught her attention. 'It kind of looked like a smudge in your sunglasses,' Isler said. 'And then, so I took my glasses off and I looked, and then I realized that it was a little girl.' That little girl was 3-year-old Luna. 'I jumped in and grabbed her' Isler said Luna was motionless at the bottom of the swimming pool when she spotted her. 'I jumped in and grabbed her and pulled her out, and she was blue,' Isler said. Isler called for her boyfriend to contact 911 and began CPR, using skills she said she learned at a young age from her parents, who both work in fire rescue. 'You just don't really think; you just kind of do, especially in a situation when it's a little baby,' Isler said. 'I pulled a lifeless baby out of a pool.' A family friend who is a pediatric intensive care unit nurse heard the commotion and joined the rescue effort, according to the account shared by Martin County Fire Rescue. 'Together, they continued their life-saving efforts till finally Luna responded,' Martin County Fire Rescue Chief Chad Cianciulli said. Fire rescue officials said Luna was alert and oriented by the time paramedics transported her to the hospital. Luna's mother says Isler was there 'at the right time' Luna's mother, Christine Hernandez, said she is grateful Isler happened to be nearby when her daughter needed help. 'It's God's work that He put her when we needed her, like at the right place at the right time,' Hernandez said. Nearly two months after that frightening day, Isler and Luna reunited at Martin County Fire Rescue headquarters. This time, they were together to celebrate the outcome of the rescue. Martin County Fire Rescue honors Isler Martin County Fire Rescue presented Isler with its Heroic Heart Award in recognition of her actions. 'Today, on behalf of Martin County Fire Rescue and our entire community, we honor Madison for her courage to act with Martin County Fire Rescue's Heroic Heart Award,' Cianciulli said during the recognition

Deputies responded around 10:17 a.m. to a home in the 7600 block of Winter Garden Boulevard, where they encountered a man in the front yard. The man went back inside after seeing law enforcement, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office . Deputies say they later contacted a man and woman at the front door. A deputy saw what appeared to be a firearm in the man's possession and ordered him to drop the weapon, but he shut the door and retreated inside, prompting a barricaded-subject situation with other occupants still in the home. See also: Driver tried to ram deputy before PIT maneuver ended chase, SLCSO says During the incident, the man reportedly came outside several times and indicated he would surrender after making a phone call, but repeatedly went back inside, deputies said.
